name: Low-cost expendable small turbojet engines (<=~400 lbf, <$100k) for low-cost cruise missiles, jet one-way-attack drones, jet interceptors and target drones
definition: IN: short-life, expendable turbojets of roughly 50-400 lbf thrust with an ASP of about $20k-100k, made by Western, allied or Ukrainian suppliers. They power $150k-$500k 'affordable mass' cruise missiles (USAF FAM, low-cost containerized munitions, ERAM, JDAM-LR, ETV, GLCM, MBDA One Way Effector), jet OWA drones, turbine interceptors and target drones. OUT: turbofans of 600 lbf and up for JASSM/LRASM/CCA (a slower, later sub-segment, split out below), hobby turbines under ~20 lbf, APUs, and Chinese/Russian/Iranian domestic engines (e.g., for the Geran-3), which Western suppliers cannot sell into.
value_chain_path: Drones & affordable mass munitions -> propulsion -> thermal propulsion -> small gas turbines -> low-cost expendable turbojets <=400 lbf (castings, bearings, ECU)
also_serves_megatrends: Low-cost cruise-missile / affordable-mass munitions rearmament (US, Europe, Taiwan/Japan)
Air & missile defense (turbine interceptors such as Coyote-class)
Munitions replenishment after the 2026 Iran conflict
Target drones for training with new air-defense systems
size_2026_usd: $0.2-0.5B (own estimate: roughly 3k-10k Western/Ukrainian units x $30-60k; supplier revenues for PBS, Williams, Safran Power Units and Collins are unverified)
volume_vs_price: Roughly 100% volume, or more. Units rise about 5-8x (from ~3-10k to ~25-60k/yr). Blended ASP falls about 5-10% a year as $50k designs (Kratos Spartan) displace legacy $150k+ missile engines and production learning sets in. Shortage pricing is not the driver: buyers are DoD cost-capped programs, so growth is durable as long as the programs fund.
math: Top-down 2030 (own estimate). US: FAM 27,000 missiles over the FYDP is ~5.4k/yr. LCCM 10,000 is ~2k/yr. ERAM, JDAM-LR, ETV, GLCM and others add 3-10k/yr. Jet OWA, target and interceptor uses add 1-3k/yr. US total: ~11-20k engines/yr. Europe, Ukraine and Asia (MBDA OWE, Ukrainian jet missile-drones, Taiwan, Japan, Korea): ~10-40k/yr. Total ~21-60k engines x ASP $35-55k = $0.75-3.3B. Bottom-up check from Kratos guidance alone: 3,000 engines x $50k = $150M in 2027 and 5,000 x $50k = $250M in 2028, with 2029 'could increase significantly'. That one supplier would equal or exceed the whole estimated 2026 Western market by 2028.
catalyst_timing: 2026-Q3/Q4: Kratos orders components for 3,000 engines for 2027 delivery. 2027: first large low-cost cruise-missile lots ('$300,000 cruise missiles beginning next year', per Kratos); ERAM deliveries to Ukraine. 2028: Kratos plans 5,000 engines; FAM rate production. Summer 2027: Kratos/GE Oklahoma turbofan plant opens (turbofans ramp 2028-29). FY27 budget: multiyear procurement authority requested for low-cost munitions.
key_suppliers: Kratos (KTOS, Nasdaq, US): Spartan turbojets, Michigan plant; also GEK 50/50 JV with GE Aerospace (GE, NYSE) for higher thrust. Williams International (private, US): incumbent in small missile engines. Collins/Pratt & Whitney TJ150 (RTX, NYSE; MALD family). Safran Power Units (SAF, Euronext Paris). PBS Aerospace / PBS Group (private, Czechia): TJ40-TJ150 series widely used in drones and targets. Hanwha Aerospace (012450.KS). US startups such as Beehive Industries (private; unverified). Ukrainian makers, e.g., Motor Sich / Ivchenko-Progress (state/private; unverified). Shares: unverified. Own estimate: incumbents (Williams, Safran, Collins, PBS) hold ~60-75% of 2026 Western value, and Kratos/GE plus startups could take 30-50% of incremental 2027-30 volume.
supply_tightness: High. Qualifying an engine into a missile takes about 18-36 months, and design wins are sticky (Kratos built its Michigan plant only after being 'designed into multiple cruise missiles'). Kratos is placing component orders 12-18 months ahead of delivery. Few qualified sources exist for small nickel-superalloy hot-section castings, high-speed hybrid ceramic bearings and small FADECs. Pricing power is limited by cost-capped government buyers, but the number of credible qualified suppliers is fewer than 10 in the West.
substitution_risk: Medium. Slow Shahed-class OWA drones use $3-15k piston engines. Short-range effectors and interceptors can use solid rockets or electric ducted fans. A turbojet is close to mandatory for 300-1,000 km subsonic cruise missiles at sub-$500k cost. Turbofans can replace turbojets where range or fuel efficiency matters (the higher-thrust class).
cyclicality_risk: Budget-driven, not consumer-cyclical. Risks: FAM/LCCM quantities cut or slipping (DoD J-book quantities often shrink); program consolidation onto fewer missiles; several new entrants overbuilding capacity for the same awards (Kratos, GE, Beehive, PBS, Hanwha, Williams); a Ukraine ceasefire reducing ERAM-type demand; cheap Chinese small turbojets pricing the non-NDAA export market.
faster_sub_niche: Split. Low-cost turbojets <=~400 lbf at ~$50k (this candidate) start ramping in 2027 at 40-65% CAGR. Small turbofans of 600 lbf and up for JASSM/LRASM/CCA carry a higher ASP but ramp later (supply chain turned on Q4-26/Q1-27, significant rates 2028-29 per Kratos) and grow more slowly over 2026-30 (own estimate 20-35%).

evidence.claim: Kratos is placing component orders for 3,000 small Spartan turbojets to be produced for customers in 2027 and plans to order components during 2027 for 5,000 more for 2028. ASP is ~$50,000. Spartan class is '250 pounds of thrust and lower', built in a new, now-operational Michigan plant. 2029 'could increase significantly'.
evidence.label: company guidance

name: Low-cost interceptor drones (<~$30k per unit) for defeating Group 2-3 one-way-attack drones
definition: IN: purpose-built drones that physically intercept hostile UAS (ram, fragment or proximity-fuze), priced at roughly $1k-30k. Examples: Ukrainian FPV/quad interceptors (Wild Hornets Sting, General Chereshnya, Skyfall) and Western low-cost interceptors (Project Eagle/Merops, Frankenburg, Nordic Air Defence, Tytan, MARSS, Origin Robotics, Cambridge Aerospace, Perennial, Anduril Anvil). Includes the interceptor airframe, seeker and fuze, and the ground C2 kit sold with it. OUT: premium turbine interceptors above ~$100k (RTX Coyote Blk2/3, the Army LRKI/AV FE-1 class), split out below; missiles (Stinger, APKWS rockets); guns; lasers; RF/cyber defeat.
value_chain_path: Drones -> counter-UAS -> kinetic defeat -> interceptor drones -> low-cost (<$30k) interceptors (airframe + EO/IR seeker + fuze + C2)
also_serves_megatrends: Air & missile defense / Golden Dome inner layer
European rearmament / EU Drone Defence Initiative ('drone wall')
Gulf-state air defense after the 2026 Iran conflict
size_2026_usd: $0.4-1.9B (own estimate; low confidence)
volume_vs_price: About 120% volume and -20% price. Units rise ~4-8x while ASP drifts down as Ukrainian-style $3-5k designs and Western $8-15k designs scale and seekers commoditise. Growth is driven by cost-exchange economics (a $3-15k interceptor against a $20-50k Shahed, instead of a $0.5-4M missile), not shortage pricing, so it is durable while the OWA threat persists.
math: 2026 (own estimate): Ukraine 100k-300k interceptors x $3-5k = $0.3-1.5B (Ukraine's stated goal of ~1,000/day is not verified as achieved), plus Western low-cost (NATO/Gulf/US pilots) ~10k-30k units x $8-15k = $0.1-0.4B. Total ~$0.4-1.9B. 2030 (own estimate): Ukraine $0.5-2B (ceasefire-sensitive), plus NATO/US/Gulf/Asia 150k-400k units x $8-15k = $1.2-6B. Total ~$2-7B. Cross-check: the AV FE-1 premium interceptor flies only in late FY27/early FY28, so the 2026-28 interceptor ramp is mostly the low-cost class.
catalyst_timing: Now to 2027: the European Drone Defence Initiative targets initial capability by end-2026 and full capability by end-2027 (memory). Post-Iran-war Gulf procurement (2026). DHS $1.5B UAS contract (Jul/Aug 2026). The US Army 1M-drone plan and DAWG FY27 funding (request) flow down from mid-2027 (6-9 month lag per Amprius). 2028+: premium Army LRKI production (AV FE-1 flight test late FY27/early FY28).
key_suppliers: Ukraine (private): Wild Hornets, General Chereshnya, Skyfall and others; fragmented, dozens of makers. Western: Project Eagle/Merops (private, US; Swift Beat), Anduril (private; Anvil/Roadrunner), Perennial Autonomy (private, US), Frankenburg Technologies (private, Estonia), Nordic Air Defence (private, Sweden), Tytan Technologies (private, Germany), Origin Robotics (private, Latvia), MARSS (private, UK/Monaco), Cambridge Aerospace (private, UK), Ondas/Iron Drone (ONDS, Nasdaq). Premium tier: RTX (RTX, NYSE; Coyote), AeroVironment (AVAV, Nasdaq; FE-1). Shares unverified; no supplier likely holds >20% of the low-cost segment.
supply_tightness: Low to medium at airframe level: easy to build, many entrants. Tighter one level down: non-Chinese thermal cores (C7) for night intercepts, NDAA-compliant cells (C4), magnets (C6), and EO/IR seekers with autonomous terminal homing. Qualification is fast (weeks to months) under Ukraine/DIU-style crucibles, so pricing power at the airframe level is weak.
substitution_risk: Medium to high. Laser and HPM systems (from 2028+), programmable airburst guns, cheaper rockets (APKWS) and better electronic warfare compete. Jet-powered Shaheds (Geran-3) raise the speed bar, favouring boosted or jet interceptors (which pulls demand toward C1 engines and the premium tier).
cyclicality_risk: High. A Ukraine ceasefire would cut the largest single demand pool. Double ordering across NATO pilots is likely. Many airframe makers could overbuild. Chinese components are cheap and keep airframe prices low. Demand is threat-driven and can fall fast if OWA drone use wanes.
faster_sub_niche: Split. Low-cost <$30k interceptors (this candidate) are ramping now. Premium turbine interceptors (Coyote Blk2/3 ~$100k+, Army LRKI/FE-1) see their production inflection about 2028+ (FE-1 flight test late FY27/early FY28), so they grow more slowly over 2026-28. Within low-cost, NATO/Gulf/US adoption is the fastest pool; Ukrainian domestic output may plateau.

evidence.claim: AV's FE-1 won a $96M US Army Long-Range Kinetic Interceptor (LRKI) development contract (fall 2025). Flight testing is expected in late FY2027 or early FY2028, so premium interceptor production comes after 2028. Management cited 'the current conflict in Iran' as a demand accelerant, and estimates a Golden Dome Limited Area Defense opportunity of ~$0.5B to AV over 3 years.

name: MANET / MIMO mesh software-defined radios for unmanned systems (OEM datalink modules and nodes)
definition: IN: wideband MIMO mesh (MANET) SDR radios and embeddable OEM modules used as C2/video/data links on UAS, UGV and USV and in the soldier/vehicle mesh that controls them: Silvus StreamCaster, Doodle Labs Mesh Rider, Persistent Systems MPU5/Wave Relay, Domo, Mobilicom and similar. OUT: legacy narrowband combat-net radios (SINCGARS etc.), SATCOM terminals, consumer/FPV links (ELRS, analog video transmitters), LTE/5G modems.
value_chain_path: Drones -> communications -> C2/data links -> MANET mesh SDR -> OEM embedded MANET modules for unmanned platforms (RF front-end + SoC-FPGA + anti-jam waveform)
size_2026_usd: $2.0-3.0B (MSI cites a ~$3B TAM; Silvus alone ~$850M company guidance)
cagr_2026_2030: 17-25% for the niche (Silvus itself grows faster through share gains)
volume_vs_price: Mostly volume: more uncrewed platforms, and more nodes per platform and per squad. ASP per node is flat to down ~5%/yr as modules shrink for attritable Group 1-2 drones. Silvus's ~80% 2026 growth is 'share gain and execution, not addressable market expansion' (MSI CEO), so it should not be read as niche growth.
math: Bottom-up 2026: Silvus ~$210M (Q1) + ~$230M (Q2), FY ~$850M (MSI guidance, capacity-limited). Persistent Systems, Doodle Labs, Domo, L3Harris mesh products, Mobilicom, Elsight and others are an unverified ~$1.0-2.0B, giving a total of ~$2-3B, consistent with MSI's ~$3B TAM. Growth: $3B doubling over 4-5 years is a 15-19% CAGR. Unit check for 2030 (own estimate): 300k-600k Group 1-3 UAS/UGV/USV with MANET x $1.5-4k module = $0.45-2.4B, plus soldier and vehicle nodes. Silvus 2025: ~$475M expected at deal announcement [STALE], so 2026 is ~+75-80%.
catalyst_timing: 2026: Silvus is capacity-constrained; MSI added a second floor in Los Angeles. Early Q1 2027: new Salt Lake City plant online. 2027: DAWG / Drone Dominance funding flow-down, Army mesh modernization, EU/German demand. Ongoing: anti-jam test results (MSI cites exceptional DoD anti-jam scores).
key_suppliers: Silvus (Motorola Solutions, MSI, NYSE; US): ~$850M 2026, about 30-40% share of the niche by own estimate. Persistent Systems (private, US): significant share, revenue unverified. Doodle Labs (private, Singapore/US): leading OEM drone module supplier, revenue unverified. Domo Tactical Communications (private, UK). L3Harris (LHX). Mobilicom (MOB, Nasdaq; small). Elsight (ELS, ASX; link bonding). Microhard (private, Canada). Rajant (private, US).
supply_tightness: Medium to high. Silvus guided FY26 'within current capacity', so production capacity is the binding constraint until 2027. The anti-jam/LPI waveform and SoC-FPGA/RF content are hard to replicate. NDAA-compliance and accreditation favour incumbents. Qualification on platforms takes 6-18 months. Pricing has held: MSI P&SI margins expanded.
substitution_risk: Medium. FPV/attritable drones increasingly use cheap ELRS-type links, fiber-optic tethers or full autonomy (no link needed for terminal attack). 5G/LTE tactical bubbles and proliferated-LEO direct links compete for some ISR backhaul. Chinese modules are cheap but excluded from US/NATO procurement.
cyclicality_risk: Medium. Defense budgets are lumpy (US 'sweeps', European tranches). Ukraine demand is war-dependent. Silvus's capacity additions in 2027 plus competitors' expansions could produce a price reset if Drone Dominance favours cheaper links.
faster_sub_niche: Embedded OEM MANET modules for attritable Group 1-2 drones grow faster in units (own estimate 30%+) but with falling ASP. Revenue CAGR is probably ~20-30%, versus ~15-19% for the overall TAM. Silvus specifically could compound 25-35% through 2028 on share gains.

evidence.claim: Silvus did about $210M in Q1-26 and ~$230M in Q2-26. MSI raised Silvus FY2026 to ~$850M (+$100M in the raise). The FY guide 'takes into account our current capacity, and we'll live within that'.

name: NDAA-compliant high-energy-density (silicon-anode) lithium-ion cells for drones and loitering munitions
definition: IN: Li-ion cells (pouch and cylindrical) at roughly 300-500 Wh/kg, or high-C high-energy cells, made in non-covered countries (US, Korea, Taiwan, Japan, EU) for UAS, loitering munitions and similar defense robotics, compliant with DoD sourcing rules (FY24 NDAA s.154 battery ban effective Oct-2027; UAS component sourcing rules). Silicon-anode cells such as Amprius SiCore are the fastest part. OUT: Chinese LiPo/Li-ion (Grepow/Tattu, Ampace, EVE), pack assembly value, EV/ESS cells, and anode-material makers (upstream).
value_chain_path: Drones -> propulsion & power -> batteries -> cells -> NDAA-compliant high-energy (Si-anode) UAS cells (built by Korean/US contract manufacturers)
also_serves_megatrends: Light e-mobility (Amprius: $21M China LEV order; Stark Future >=$100M through 2029)
Data-center rack-level power smoothing (exploratory, per Amprius CFO)
size_2026_usd: $0.35-0.8B (own estimate; Amprius >= $140M company guidance is the only verified anchor)
volume_vs_price: About 75% volume and 25% price/mix. Volume comes from Group 1-3 military and commercial UAS shifting to non-Chinese cells after Oct-2027. Price/mix comes from the NDAA compliance premium (Amprius CFO: NDAA 'comes with a different cost structure that we need to be paid for') and the shift toward custom pouch cells (high-30s gross margin versus low-20s for cylindrical). The premium is regulatory and therefore durable, not shortage pricing.
math: Bottom-up 2026: Amprius >=$140M (Q2 run-rate $136M). Molicel (Taiwan Cement subsidiary) drone/eVTOL high-power cells, Korean incumbents' drone-specific sales, Saft/EaglePicher/Epsilor military small-UAS cells and Enovix defense together add an unverified ~$0.2-0.65B. Total ~$0.35-0.8B. Top-down 2030 (own estimate): NDAA-relevant small-UAS demand (US + NATO + allies) 1-2M Group 1-2 airframes/yr x ~0.3 kWh = 0.3-0.6 GWh; Group 2-3 + loitering munitions + defense robots 0.3-0.8 GWh; US commercial/public-safety drones post FCC action 0.2-0.5 GWh. Total ~0.8-1.9 GWh x $1,000-1,500/kWh premium cell price = $0.8-2.9B. Amprius itself targets '>$600M of contracted capacity' by decade-end, about 4x 2026.
catalyst_timing: Late Jul/Aug 2026: Drone Dominance Gauntlet II at Fort Carson (19 OEMs, ~half on Amprius cells); DoD orders 60,000 drones from top performers. Dec-2026: Amprius Fremont DIU-funded NDAA pilot line starts production. 2027: Amprius fully domestic NDAA cells. Oct 1, 2027: FY24 NDAA s.154 bars DoD procurement of batteries from CATL, BYD, Envision, EVE, Gotion and Hithium. Mid-2027: FY27 DAWG funds flow down (6-9 month lag). 2027-28: 'stricter domestic requirements' for military and commercial drones (analyst framing on the Amprius call).
key_suppliers: Amprius (AMPX, NYSE; US): SiCore; Korean contract manufacturers Libest, JR Energy and Top Material; US contract manufacturer Nanotech Energy (private). Molicel / E-One Moli (subsidiary of Taiwan Cement, 1101.TW). Samsung SDI (006400.KS) and LG Energy Solution (373220.KS): high-power 21700 cells used in drones. Enovix (ENVX, Nasdaq; Routejade Korea). Saft (TotalEnergies, TTE). EaglePicher (private, US). Epsilor (Israel). Lyten (private; Li-S, later). Shares unverified. Own estimate: Amprius ~20-35% of the 2026 non-Chinese high-energy UAS cell niche.
supply_tightness: High. Setting up NDAA-compliant capacity takes 1-2 years (Amprius CFO). Amprius had to qualify two sets of 11 new component suppliers (anode, cathode, separator, binders). Domestic US pouch capacity is still being established. Cell-level qualification and flight-time 'shootouts' make customers sticky: Amprius cells can deliver '50% better or more' flight time.
substitution_risk: Medium. Korean/Japanese majors could target the niche with conventional high-nickel cells. Chinese semi-solid cells are cheaper but excluded from DoD buys after 2027. Li-S and solid-state (2028+) could leapfrog. Hybrid/heavy-fuel power for Group 3. Fiber-optic FPVs do not change battery demand.
cyclicality_risk: Medium. Defense funding lags (6-9 months). A Ukraine/Europe demand dip (68% of Amprius Q2 revenue came from EMEA). Repurposed idle EV cell capacity in the US could flood the market if many players chase the NDAA niche.
faster_sub_niche: US-made (domestic) NDAA-compliant silicon-anode pouch cells. Near zero in 2026 (Fremont pilot line from Dec-2026; Nanotech cylindrical) and could reach $0.3-1B by 2030 (60%+ CAGR, emerging). Korean-made NDAA cells are the bridge supply.

evidence.claim: Q2-26 revenue was $34.0M (+19% q/q, 2.3x y/y). H1-26 revenue was $62.6M (+137% y/y). Gross margin was 27%. SiCore was 98% of revenue and EMEA 68%. FY2026 guidance raised to at least $140M with gross margin of at least 28%.
evidence.label: reported fact
evidence.source: Amprius Technologies Q2 2026 earnings call transcript (Alpha Vantage)

evidence.claim: DoD's Drone Dominance program invited 19 drone makers to a competitive demonstration at Fort Carson. Half of them use Amprius cells. DoD will order 60,000 drones from the top performers. The FY2027 request seeks >$50B for the Defense Autonomous Warfare Group. These are the CEO's characterizations; the budget figure is not independently verified.
evidence.label: reported fact
evidence.source: Amprius Q2 2026 earnings call transcript (CEO remarks)

evidence.claim: NDAA-compliant capacity has a 1-2 year lead time. Amprius qualified two sets of 11 new suppliers, expects full US-domestic NDAA-compliant cells in 2027, and has access to >2 GWh/yr of capacity (12-15M cells/quarter). Its decade-end target is >$600M of contracted capacity, gross margin above 30% and adjusted EBITDA margin of at least 20%.
evidence.label: company guidance

evidence.claim: FY2024 NDAA section 154 prohibits DoD procurement of batteries from CATL, BYD, Envision, EVE, Gotion and Hithium starting Oct 1, 2027. From memory, not re-fetched.
evidence.label: reported fact
evidence.source: National Defense Authorization Act for FY2024 (H.R.2670), section 154

evidence.claim: Amprius received a $24M order from a new European drone OEM (SA124 cylindrical, delivering over ~2.5 quarters). Customer Redwire won >$40M of USMC purchase orders for the Stalker Block 30, which uses Amprius cells.
evidence.label: reported fact

notes: A strong deep-chain candidate with a hard regulatory catalyst inside the window (Oct-2027), real capacity lead times, and demand from four or more megatrends. The main unknown is the size of non-Amprius competitors (Molicel's drone share, Korean majors). Check Taiwan (Taiwan Cement/Molicel IR, MoneyDJ) and Korean (The Elec) sources when the search budget allows.

name: Domestic public-safety and critical-infrastructure counter-UAS: RF detection plus cyber-takeover mitigation
definition: IN: fixed, mobile and portable systems (hardware plus software/subscription) that detect, track and identify drones by RF/protocol analysis and mitigate them non-kinetically by protocol/cyber takeover or legally authorised RF defeat. Buyers are law enforcement, DHS/DOJ, prisons, airports, stadiums/events, utilities, nuclear sites and data centers. Examples: D-Fend EnforceAir, Dedrone, DroneShield fixed/handheld, Sentrycs, MyDefence, Hidden Level. OUT: battlefield RF jammers (split out, see overhyped), radar-only and kinetic/laser systems.
value_chain_path: Drones -> counter-UAS -> non-kinetic defeat -> RF/protocol detection + cyber-takeover -> domestic public-safety & critical-infrastructure deployments (sensors + SaaS)
also_serves_megatrends: Airport resilience after the 2025 European airport drone closures
size_2026_usd: $0.4-0.8B (own estimate; D-Fend ~$185M company guidance is the verified anchor)
volume_vs_price: About 85% volume (new sites and agencies as legal authority expands) and 15% price/mix (shift to recurring software subscriptions and multi-sensor sites). ASP per site is roughly stable. Growth is driven by authority, grants and threat, not shortage.
math: Bottom-up 2026: D-Fend ~$185M (MSI). Dedrone (Axon), DroneShield's civil share, Sentrycs (Ondas), MyDefence, Hidden Level, Rohde & Schwarz and Hensoldt's civil share add an unverified ~$0.25-0.6B. Total ~$0.4-0.8B. Top-down 2030 (own estimate): US + EU + Gulf addressable sites. ~1,000-2,000 large law-enforcement agencies, ~1,900 prisons, ~500 commercial airports, ~1,000+ stadiums/venues, 90+ nuclear plants, thousands of substations and data centers. Assume ~10-20k deployed sites x $50-250k hardware amortised plus SaaS = $1.5-3B/yr. D-Fend's historical ~50% 3-year CAGR (MSI) bounds the upside.
catalyst_timing: Late Jul/Aug 2026: DHS $1.5B UAS contract; D-Fend the sole cyber-mitigation vendor selected (MSI). H2-2026: MSI closes the $1.5B D-Fend deal, bringing its global distribution. The FY2026 NDAA (Dec-2025) reportedly expanded C-UAS mitigation authority, including state/local pathways (memory, re-verify). 2026-2028: post-World Cup lessons (about 700 drones detected), LA28 Olympics procurement, EU airport programs.
key_suppliers: D-Fend Solutions (Israel; being acquired by Motorola Solutions, MSI). Dedrone (Axon, AXON, Nasdaq). DroneShield (DRO, ASX; Australia). AeroVironment Titan (AVAV; mainly military). Sentrycs (Ondas, ONDS). MyDefence (private, Denmark). Hidden Level (private, US). Rohde & Schwarz ARDRONIS (private, Germany). Hensoldt (HAG, Xetra). Fortem (private, US; DroneHunter, kinetic net). Shares unverified. Own estimate: D-Fend and Dedrone together ~35-50% of the domestic cyber/RF segment.

name: US-made sintered NdFeB permanent magnets (incl. Dy/Tb high-temperature grades for drone, munition, EV and robot motors)
definition: IN: sintered NdFeB magnets produced in the United States (MP Materials Independence/10X, eVAC Sumter, Noveon, USA Rare Earth Stillwater, Vulcan Elements), sold as finished magnets. Grain-boundary-diffused Dy/Tb grades for high-temperature motors are included. OUT: bonded NdFeB, SmCo, upstream oxide/metal (except where vertically integrated), and Chinese or Japanese production. The broader ex-China parent (Japan/EU/Korea/Vietnam) is split out below as the slower sub-segment.
value_chain_path: Drones -> propulsion -> brushless motors -> permanent magnets -> sintered NdFeB -> US-made (DFARS/10 USC 4872-compliant) sintered NdFeB
also_serves_megatrends: EV traction motors (GM, Apple and other US offtakes)
Data-center cooling fans / HDD voice-coil motors
size_2026_usd: $0.1-0.4B (own estimate; ~1-3k t shipped x ~$80-150/kg)
volume_vs_price: About 75% volume (new US plants ramping from ~1-3k t to ~8-20k t) and 25% price (ex-China premium underwritten by the DoD NdPr floor of $110/kg and long-term offtakes). The premium is policy-created; if China relaxes controls, open-market premiums compress, but DoD/OEM offtakes keep most volume contracted.
math: Bottom-up capacity (memory, unverified current status). MP Independence ~1,000 t/yr ramping 2025-26, plus 10X ~7,000 t targeted 2028. eVAC Sumter ~1,500 t. Noveon ~2,000 t. USA Rare Earth phase-1 ~1,200 t (2026), up to ~4,800 t. Vulcan Elements 10,000 t (post-2027). Realistic 2030 shipments are ~8-20k t, below nameplate, x $90-140/kg = $0.7-2.8B. 2026 shipments ~1-3k t x $80-150/kg = $0.1-0.45B. Drone share check: a quad uses ~40-200 g of magnet, so 5M drones/yr need only ~200-1,000 t. Drones are a strategic but minority driver; EV, defense and robots dominate volume.
catalyst_timing: Jan 1, 2027: 10 USC 4872 bars DoD from acquiring magnets with any covered-nation mining, refining, alloying or sintering in the chain. ~Nov 2026: one-year suspension of China's Oct-2025 export-control expansion lapses (re-escalation risk). 2026-27: MP Independence full ramp; USAR Stillwater commissioning. 2028: MP 10X start-up. 2028-29: Vulcan scale-up.
key_suppliers: MP Materials (MP, NYSE; US): vertically integrated; DoD anchor investor. Vulcan Elements (private, US). USA Rare Earth (USAR, Nasdaq). eVAC / VAC (private, Germany/US). Noveon Magnetics (private, US; recycled feed). Arnold Magnetic (private, US; mostly SmCo). Ex-China parent: Shin-Etsu Chemical (4063.T), TDK (6762.T), Proterial (private, Japan), Star Group (Korea), Neo Performance Materials (NEO.TO; Narva, Estonia). Own estimate of US 2026 share: MP + eVAC + Noveon >80%.
supply_tightness: Very high. China holds ~90% of global sintered magnet output. A new magnet plant takes 2-4 years to build and 12-24 months to qualify with OEMs for automotive/defense PPAP. Dy/Tb heavy-REE supply outside China is minimal. Teledyne says >$1B of its own revenue depends on germanium and rare-earth magnet supply.
substitution_risk: Low to medium within the window. Ferrite or induction motors for some EV uses. Iron-nitride magnets (Niron) are early. Heavy-REE-free grades reduce Dy/Tb but not NdFeB. For small drones, NdFeB is effectively irreplaceable for power density.
cyclicality_risk: Medium to high. If China durably relaxes controls, the commercial (non-DoD) premium could collapse and stall US projects without offtakes. Several projects targeting 2028-29 nameplate could overbuild relative to qualified demand. NdPr price volatility.
faster_sub_niche: Split. US-made sintered NdFeB (this candidate) at 45-75% CAGR, versus the total ex-China sintered NdFeB parent (~$1.2-2.4B in 2026, own estimate) at ~15-25%, since Japanese incumbents grow slowly. Within US output, Dy/Tb GBD high-temperature grades for defense and drones are the tightest, given the heavy-REE scarcity outside China.

name: Broadband direct-to-device (D2D) satellite-to-smartphone service: wholesale and OEM-funded revenue
definition: IN: satellite-operator revenue for service delivered directly to unmodified smartphones or standard 3GPP NTN devices. This covers MNO wholesale fees and revenue shares (T-Mobile and other partners with Starlink Direct to Cell; AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone, Rakuten and stc with AST SpaceMobile), OEM-funded capacity (Apple with Globalstar), standards-based NB-/NR-NTN service (Iridium NTN Direct, Skylo, Lynk/Omnispace) and government D2D. OUT: legacy dedicated sat-phone MSS handsets (Iridium, Inmarsat, Thuraya), satellite IoT modules, spectrum-sale proceeds and the MNO's retail mark-up. SPLIT: emergency SOS/messaging (low ARPU, often bundled free) vs broadband voice/data (Starlink next-gen D2C on EchoStar spectrum, AST Block 2). The broadband part is faster and is the core of this niche.
value_chain_path: Space & satellites -> Satellite services -> Mobile satellite services (MSS) -> Direct-to-device (unmodified handsets) -> Broadband voice/data D2D wholesale to MNOs (Starlink D2C next-gen, AST BlueBird Block 2)
size_2026_usd: $0.4-0.9B (own estimate, bottom-up from supplier revenues). The broadband-only sub-segment is about $0.15-0.4B (own estimate).
volume_vs_price: About 85-95% of growth is volume: paying or covered users, countries switched on and constellation capacity. ASP per user is flat to down because D2D is bundled into premium plans (T-Mobile charges $10/month standalone and includes it free in top plans). The growth is not shortage pricing. Spectrum scarcity supports the wholesale share, but Starlink's scale is likely to compress wholesale rates after 2028.
math:
2026 bottom-up (own estimates):
- Globalstar wholesale capacity (Apple-funded): $170-230M, assuming 60-80% of a ~$280-310M revenue run-rate (unverified split).
- Starlink D2C wholesale: $100-350M, from about 2-5M paying-equivalent users across T-Mobile and ~10 international MNOs at $3-6/month wholesale.
- AST SpaceMobile: $80-250M, extrapolated from H2-2025 guidance of $50-75M (gateway/equipment, government, early service; unverified).
- Iridium NTN Direct, Skylo, Lynk/Omnispace, Tiantong: $30-100M.
- Total: ~$0.4-0.9B.
2030 top-down: partner-MNO subscriber base of 3-5B x 3-6% paid attach = 100-250M users x $1.5-3/month wholesale ($18-36/year) = $1.8-9B. Trimmed to $2.5-7B for capacity limits: Starlink's next-gen D2C needs Starship (~2027+), and AST needs ~90+ satellites for continuous coverage.
CAGR check: central 0.6 -> 4.5 = ~65%; low 0.9 -> 2.5 = ~29%; high 0.4 -> 7 = ~104%.
catalyst_timing:
Timeline:
- 2024-11: FCC grants the first SCS authorisation (SpaceX/T-Mobile).
- 2025-07: T-Satellite goes commercial.
- 2025-10: data and apps added on T-Satellite (unverified).
- 2025-09 and 2025-11: SpaceX buys EchoStar spectrum. FCC transfer approval and closing are expected in 2026 (unverified).
- 2025-26: AST Block 2 launches, with a target of 45-60 satellites by end-2026 (company guidance, unverified). This enables near-continuous US/EU service in 2026-27.
- ~2027-28: Starlink next-gen D2C satellites on the new spectrum, launched by Starship.
- 2026-27: 3GPP Rel-19 NR-NTN handset support.
key_suppliers:
Estimated revenue shares are own estimates.
- SpaceX / Starlink Direct to Cell (private, US): ~25-40% in 2026, rising to ~50-70% by 2030.
- Globalstar (GSAT; Apple holds ~20%): ~30-45% in 2026.
- AST SpaceMobile (ASTS, Nasdaq): ~10-25%.
- Iridium (IRDM, Nasdaq): NTN Direct.
- Skylo (private, US/India): NB-NTN for Pixel, Samsung and Verizon.
- Lynk Global + Omnispace (private, merging; SES-backed).
- China Telecom Tiantong (0728.HK / 601728.SS): closed domestic market, Huawei handsets.
- Satellite builders: SpaceX and AST in-house (Midland, TX); MDA Space (MDA.TO) builds Globalstar's replacement satellites.
supply_tightness: The binding constraints are spectrum and launch, not components. SpaceX paid ~$17B for EchoStar AWS-4/H-block and ~$2.6B for AWS-3 unpaired spectrum (2025), which shows the scarcity value of MSS-capable spectrum. AST relies on Ligado L-band, S-band rights and partner MNO low-band. Launch slots (Falcon 9, New Glenn, LVM3) gate AST's ramp. Only 2-3 Western operators can deliver broadband D2D before 2028, so this is an oligopoly, but pricing is set by MNO bundling.
substitution_risk:
- Terrestrial coverage build-out and free bundling (Apple SOS) cap ARPU.
- SpaceX could go retail, using EchoStar spectrum to sell mobile service itself. That moves the pool from wholesale to retail and changes who captures it, but not its size.
- Cheaper GEO NB-NTN messaging (Viasat/Inmarsat, EchoStar) competes at the low end.
cyclicality_risk:
There is no double-ordering. The risks are:
- Capacity overbuild and a price war between Starlink and AST/others from about 2028.
- Regulatory risk: FCC power/out-of-band emission limits and interference objections from MNOs.
- China is a separate, closed market.
faster_sub_niche: Broadband voice/data D2D (Starlink next-gen D2C, AST Block 2) grows from ~$0.15-0.4B at an estimated 70-120% CAGR. Emergency SOS/messaging (Apple-Globalstar, Skylo) grows ~15-30% because it is bundled free. Broadband is higher-ARPU and replaces rural roaming/coverage spend, so it is the part analysed as the growth core.

name: On-robot embodied-AI compute modules (>=100 TOPS SoMs) for humanoids, quadrupeds and mobile manipulators
definition: IN: merchant system-on-modules and SoCs of 100+ INT8 TOPS that run perception and VLA policies on the robot itself: NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX/AGX and Jetson Thor (T5000-class), Horizon RDK S100-class, Qualcomm IQ-series, Ambarella robotics SoCs. Applications: humanoids, quadrupeds, mobile manipulators, AMRs, industrial edge-AI cells. OUT: automotive ADAS/robotaxi SoCs, Tesla's captive AI4/AI5 (noted separately), sub-100 TOPS SoCs (RK3588-class), cloud training GPUs.
value_chain_path: Robotics & humanoids -> humanoid/mobile robot -> compute & software -> on-robot inference compute -> >=100 TOPS SoM (Jetson Thor-class) -> [Blackwell GPU / BPU SoC + LPDDR5X]
size_2026_usd: $150-450M (own estimate; mid about $250M; NVIDIA does not disclose Jetson revenue)
volume_vs_price: Units rise from about 0.2-0.35M (2026) to 1.2-2.5M (2030), about 50% unit CAGR. For humanoids, ASP rises with each generation: Orin NX at about $500-700 vs Jetson Thor T5000 at $2,999 list (1k units). AMR modules deflate. Blended ASP is flat to +5% a year, so growth is about 85% volume and 15% rising content.
math: 2026: humanoids 40-70k x 60-80% using a 100+ TOPS merchant module x $600-2,000 = $15-110M; quadrupeds, mobile manipulators, AMRs and industrial edge 150-300k x $400-1,000 = $60-300M. Total $75-410M (mid about $250M). 2030: humanoids 400k-1.0M x 55-65% merchant (Tesla captive excluded) x $1,000-2,000 = $0.22-1.3B; other robots 1.0-2.0M x $400-800 = $0.4-1.6B. catalyst_timing: Jetson Thor (Blackwell) has shipped since Aug 2025 (dev kit $3,499; T5000 $2,999 at 1k units); lower-cost Thor variants in 2026 are unverified. VLA foundation models (GR00T N-series, Gemini Robotics, pi-0.5-class) move on-device in 2026-28. Safety-certified NVIDIA stack (Halos) from 2026. Horizon/D-Robotics RDK platforms serve Chinese OEMs.
key_suppliers: NVIDIA (NVDA; Jetson; est. 60-75% of merchant 100+ TOPS robot-compute value, own estimate, unverified); Horizon Robotics (9660.HK) via D-Robotics (about 40% retained stake); Qualcomm (QCOM); Ambarella (AMBA; more than 15 robotics design wins); Black Sesame (2533.HK; robotics traction unverified). supply_tightness: Not capacity-constrained: mature TSMC nodes and adequate LPDDR5X supply. cyclicality_risk: Moderate. Tied to robot volumes; export-control shocks. 2025-26 dev-kit buying by labs can inflate early numbers (double-counting prototypes).
faster_sub_niche: Humanoid on-robot compute (Thor-class, more than 1,000 FP4 TFLOPS) grows about 70-90% vs AMR/industrial edge at about 25-35%. The humanoid slice is under $0.1B in 2026, i.e. emerging on its own.

name: Outsourced commercial-scale peptide API for next-wave (non-Lilly/Novo) incretin and amylin drugs
definition: GMP drug-substance manufacturing done by CDMOs (SPPS or hybrid SPPS/LPPS synthesis, prep RP-HPLC purification, isolation) for GLP-1/GIP/glucagon/amylin peptides owned by sponsors other than Lilly and Novo. Examples: survodutide (BI/Zealand), VK2735 (Viking), MET-097i/MET-233i (Pfizer via Metsera), petrelintide (Roche/Zealand), HRS9531 (Kailera/Hengrui), ecnoglutide (Sciwind), AbbVie/Gubra amylin. IN: phase-3, process-validation, launch and commercial supply, plus capacity-reservation fees and prepayments. OUT: CDMO overflow supply of tirzepatide/semaglutide/retatrutide for Lilly/Novo (the slower sub-segment), generic merchant API, recombinant or antibody obesity biologics (MariTide), finished dose.
value_chain_path: Obesity/incretin drugs -> drug substance (API) -> synthetic peptide API (SPPS/hybrid) -> outsourced CDMO manufacturing -> next-wave innovator incretin/amylin programs (non-Lilly/Novo)
also_serves_megatrends: Other therapeutic peptides (oncology, rare disease) using the same large-scale SPPS capacity
size_2026_usd: $0.25-0.6B (own estimate built from supplier revenue anchors; no supplier discloses this segment directly)
size_2030_usd: $0.5-1.5B (own estimate; base case ~$1.0B if 3-5 next-wave programs launch by 2029)
volume_vs_price: Volume drives more than all of the growth (roughly 120-150% of it). API kg could rise 35-60%/yr as programs move from phase 3 to commercial. That is partly offset by price per kg falling 5-10%/yr as batches scale and new capacity arrives (WuXi >100 kL SPPS, CordenPharma, Bachem, PolyPeptide, Chinese makers). Reservation fees and prepayments prop up 2026-27 pricing but will not last.
math: Bottom-up 2026 (own estimate). Global outsourced peptide API revenue is roughly $3-4.5B: WuXi TIDES run-rate ~RMB 10-12B (H1-2025 reported RMB 5.03B, includes oligos); Bachem ~CHF 0.6-0.75B; PolyPeptide ~EUR 0.34-0.42B; CordenPharma, Asymchem, ScinoPharm, Sinopep, Hybio, AmbioPharm, Olon, Ajinomoto, Neuland and others ~$0.8-1.2B. Incretin share ~50-65% -> $1.7-2.8B. Next-wave sponsors' clinical, validation and launch supply ~15-25% of that -> $0.25-0.6B. Top-down 2030: 3-5 launches (survodutide, VK2735, MET-097i, petrelintide, Chinese assets) reach 1.5-5M patient-years. API per patient-year 0.2-0.8 g (2-15 mg weekly doses) x 1.3 for yield and inventory -> 0.4-5 t. At $100-250k/kg CDMO pricing (own assumption, unverified) that is $0.1-1.2B commercial, plus $0.2-0.4B clinical/PPQ supply for the next programs -> $0.5-1.5B. Midpoints $0.4B -> $1.0B = ~26% CAGR. Cross-check: one prepayment-backed reservation (Viking-CordenPharma) at an assumed 200-500 kg/yr (unverified) would cover ~0.4-1.5M patient-years.
catalyst_timing: BI survodutide phase-3 (SYNCHRONIZE) readouts 2026 -> filing 2026/27 -> launch 2027/28. Viking VK2735 phase 3 (VANQUISH, started mid-2025) data ~2027 -> launch 2028/29. Pfizer/Metsera MET-097i phase 3 2026 -> launch ~2028/29. Roche/Zealand petrelintide phase 3 from 2026 -> ~2029/30. Chinese next-wave (mazdutide approved in China June 2025) 2026-28. Validation campaigns run 12-18 months ahead of launch, so CDMO revenue inflects 2026-2028. Timelines are recalled, not re-verified.
key_suppliers: WuXi TIDES unit of WuXi AppTec (603259.SS / 2359.HK, China): largest large-scale SPPS capacity, est. 25-40% of global large-scale peptide CDMO revenue (own estimate); US-sponsor access may be limited by BIOSECURE-type rules (status unverified). Bachem (BANB.SW, Switzerland; est. 15-20%). PolyPeptide (PPGN.SW, Sweden/Belgium/US; est. 8-12%). CordenPharma (private/Astorg, CH/DE/US; est. 8-12%; VK2735 supplier). Also: Asymchem (002821.SZ / 6821.HK), ScinoPharm (1789.TW), Sinopep-Allsino (688076.SS), Hybio (300199.SZ), AmbioPharm (private, US/CN), Olon (private, IT), Ajinomoto Bio-Pharma (2802.T), and Neuland (NEULANDLAB.NS) / Divi's (DIVISLAB.NS) for fragments. Amneal (AMRX) is reportedly building peptide and fill-finish capacity with Metsera (unverified). All shares are own estimates.
supply_tightness: Few CDMOs can run multi-ton/yr GMP SPPS with matching prep-HPLC trains. A new large-scale building takes ~3-4 years (design, build, qualification, PPQ). Switching CDMO after approval needs comparability data plus a prior-approval supplement or variation (12-24 months), so sponsors lock in 2-3 years before launch and pay prepayments or take-or-pay (e.g., Viking-CordenPharma). Tight through ~2027. Risk of loosening from 2028 as WuXi (>100,000 L SPPS target), CordenPharma (EUR ~900M program), Bachem (Bubendorf/Sisslen) and Chinese generics makers add capacity.
substitution_risk: Medium. Oral small molecules (orforglipron and followers) and monthly biologics (MariTide) cap injectable peptide growth. Well-funded sponsors (Pfizer, Roche) may bring production in-house after launch. Recombinant expression could undercut SPPS for long peptides. Each phase-3 failure removes its demand outright.
cyclicality_risk: Medium-high. In 2024-26 sponsors double-booked capacity across several CDMOs as a hedge. Overbuild in China (WuXi, Asymchem, Hybio, Sinopep) plus Western expansions could squeeze prices in 2028-29. Demand is lumpy (PPQ campaigns, launch stocking).
faster_sub_niche: Outsourced incretin API splits three ways: (i) Lilly/Novo overflow (tirzepatide etc.), likely 0-15% CAGR as Lilly's >$50B US build and Novo's in-house recombinant semaglutide capacity come online; (ii) next-wave sponsors (kept here, 15-40%); (iii) generic merchant API (high volume, falling price, low $ value). Within (ii), amylin analogs (petrelintide, MET-233i, AbbVie GUB014295) grow fastest but only inflect 2028-30 (see too_early).

name: Preparative RP-HPLC bonded spherical silica for peptide (GLP-1/amylin) API purification
definition: Bulk spherical high-purity silica (typically 10-20 um particles, 100-120 A pores; C4/C8/C18-bonded or unbonded), sold by the kg or ton to pack industrial dynamic-axial-compression columns (0.3-1.6 m inner diameter) for GMP purification of incretin and amylin peptide APIs. OUT: analytical and semi-prep columns, polymeric RP and ion-exchange resins, Protein A, chiral stationary phases. Insulin and small-molecule prep use is noted only as slower-growing context.
value_chain_path: Obesity/incretin drugs -> peptide API manufacturing -> downstream purification -> preparative reversed-phase HPLC -> bonded spherical silica media (peptide end-use)
also_serves_megatrends: Other therapeutic peptides (oncology, rare disease, radioligand precursors)
size_2026_usd: $0.15-0.35B for peptide end-use; $0.3-0.6B including insulin and small-molecule prep (own estimate, low confidence; no supplier discloses segment revenue)
volume_vs_price: Mostly volume. Peptide API tonnage could grow 30-50%/yr (oral semaglutide 25 mg, higher injectable doses, generics, combinations). But silica consumed per kg of API falls (longer media life, purer crude from hybrid/LPPS, continuous MCSGP), and Chinese suppliers push price down ~2-5%/yr. First-fill demand from the 2024-27 capacity build does not recur.
math: Consumption model (own estimate): loading 5-20 g peptide per litre of bed per cycle; media life 100-300 cycles; packed density ~0.5-0.6 kg/L; 2 RP passes; 70-85% step yield -> ~0.4-2 kg silica per kg of final API. RP-purified peptide/insulin tonnage 2026 ~40-80 t (semaglutide incl. Rybelsus/oral Wegovy ~10-25 t; tirzepatide ~4-8 t; insulins ~25-40 t; others) -> 20-160 t replacement media. First fills add more: each 0.8-1.6 m column holds ~150-800 kg, and the 2024-27 build-out adds an estimated 50-150 t/yr. Total 70-300 t x $1.5-3.5k/kg (bonded prep silica price, unverified) -> $0.1-1.0B; central case ~$0.25-0.45B all end-uses. 2030: oral semaglutide 25 mg daily = 9.1 g API per patient-year vs 0.125 g for 2.4 mg weekly injection (73x). 2-4M oral patient-years would need 18-36 t of semaglutide alone. Total peptide tonnage 120-250 t -> 50-500 t replacement silica; first fills level off -> peptide end-use $0.35-0.8B, i.e. 12-25% CAGR. The low end applies if MCSGP and hybrid routes cut media per kg by 30-50%.
catalyst_timing: Oral Wegovy 25 mg approved by FDA Dec 2025, US launch Jan 2026, ex-US 2026-27. Semaglutide 7.2 mg dose. Generic semaglutide in CN/IN/BR/CA from 2026. New-entrant PPQ campaigns 2026-28. Retatrutide launch ~2027. Media demand lags API tonnage by 0-12 months (columns are first filled at PPQ).
key_suppliers: Nouryon Kromasil (private, Bohus, Sweden; est. 25-35% of industrial RP silica); Osaka Soda Daisogel (4046.T, Japan; est. 15-25%); YMC (private, Kyoto; est. 10-20%; also MCSGP via ChromaCon); AGC Si-Tech (AGC 5201.T; est. 5-10%); Fuji Silysia (private, Japan); Merck KGaA (MRK.DE); W.R. Grace Davisil (private, US); Suzhou Nanomicro (688690.SS, China; est. 5-10%, rising with Chinese generics). All shares are own estimates, unverified.
supply_tightness: Spherical sol-gel silica is made in quality-critical batches (metal impurities, particle-size distribution, bonding reproducibility); new lines take ~2-3 years. The media grade is written into the CMC dossier, so changing supplier after approval needs comparability data and often a regulatory variation; incumbents usually keep a product for its whole life. Lead times stretched during the 2024-25 GLP-1 ramp, and Osaka Soda and Nouryon added capacity (magnitudes unverified).
substitution_risk: Medium. Polymeric RP media (higher pH tolerance, longer life), MCSGP continuous chromatography, and higher-purity crude from hybrid/LPPS all reduce media per kg. Low-price Chinese silica (Nanomicro) wins domestic generics.
cyclicality_risk: Medium-high. First-fill orders track the 2024-27 peptide capex wave and could stall in 2028-29. Stock built during the 2024-25 shortage scare may unwind.

name: Oral small-molecule GLP-1 RA API and advanced intermediates (orforglipron first)
definition: Drug substance and late-stage intermediates (from regulatory starting materials onward) for non-peptide oral GLP-1 receptor agonists. size_2026_usd: $0.15-0.4B production value including captive Lilly API and launch inventory; outsourced CDMO portion ~$0.05-0.2B (own estimates; the merchant-only portion may be below $50M, i.e. emerging)

volume_vs_price: Volume drives more than all of the growth: API tonnage could go from single-digit tons to 30-110 t/yr. Cost per kg should fall 30-50% through process learning and scale, so revenue grows slower than tonnage. There is no shortage pricing because small-molecule capacity is interchangeable.
math: Top-down 2030 (own estimate): 4-10M orforglipron patient-years globally (US Medicare/TrumpRx pricing from $149/month, plus ex-US and emerging markets where no cold chain is needed) x average 20-30 mg/day (dose range 3-36 mg) = 7.3-11 g per patient-year -> 30-110 t API, plus 10-20% for yield and inventory. At $3-12k/kg (own assumption for a complex multi-step small molecule, unverified) -> $0.1-1.3B; followers add under $0.1B by 2030. 2026: 0.5-1.5M patient-years -> 4-16 t demand plus inventory build. Lilly's ~$0.55B of pre-launch orforglipron inventory reported in 2025 filings (recalled) implies several hundred $M of API and tablet production before launch. The outsourced share is 30-60% until Lilly's Houston API plant (announced at $6.5B, ~2030) brings work in-house.
catalyst_timing: US obesity approval was expected in 2026 under the FDA national priority voucher; an April 2026 approval under the brand name 'Foundayo' is recalled but unverified. T2D filing 2026; ex-US launches 2026-27; Medicare obesity coverage from mid-2026 under the Nov-2025 pricing deal; Houston API plant online ~2029-30 (moves production in-house); followers' phase-3 readouts 2027-28.
key_suppliers: Eli Lilly (LLY) captive API (US/Ireland sites; Houston TX plant under construction). Chugai (4519.T) is the originator and holds royalties; it is not a supplier. supply_tightness: Low-moderate. Generic small-molecule capacity is ample. The bottleneck is the filed route and its qualified intermediates (regulatory starting-material suppliers are locked into the NDA). CDMOs have little pricing power, and Lilly dual-sources.
substitution_risk: Medium-high. Competition comes from oral semaglutide 25 mg (similar efficacy), cheaper injectables (US deals at $245-350/month) and next-generation orals. There is also class safety risk: Pfizer dropped danuglipron in 2025 after a liver-injury signal.
cyclicality_risk: High. Pre-launch stockpiling (2024-26) is followed by destocking; demand for outsourced work steps down when Houston starts; competing followers arrive from 2029.
faster_sub_niche: Outsourced advanced intermediates grow fastest in 2026-2029, then slow once Houston brings production in-house. Followers' API is too early (2029+).

name: Outsourced platform pen-injectors and autoinjectors for incretin drugs (generic + next-wave)
definition: Disposable multi-dose pen-injectors and single-dose autoinjectors that independent device makers design, make and customise for pharma customers. They are used on GLP-1/incretin products other than Novo's and Lilly's own captive devices: generic liraglutide/semaglutide pens, Chinese and Indian brands, and next-wave innovators (e.g., VK2735, MET-097i, survodutide). value_chain_path: Obesity/incretin drugs -> drug product & delivery -> self-injection devices -> outsourced platform pens/autoinjectors -> incretin generics & next-wave innovators
size_2026_usd: $0.3-0.7B (own estimate)
volume_vs_price: About 90% or more of growth is volume: generic semaglutide multi-dose pens in the markets that lost exclusivity in 2026 (1 pen/month) and new-entrant autoinjectors (weekly or monthly). ASPs are flat to falling because generic customers are price-sensitive (own estimate ~$1.5-3 per multi-dose pen, ~$3-6 per autoinjector).
math: 2026 unit context (own estimate): ~600-750M incretin pens/autoinjectors globally, ~85-90% of them captive (Novo FlexTouch ~350-450M; Lilly KwikPen and single-dose pen ~200-250M; plus ~100M Lilly vials). Outsourced 2026: generic liraglutide/semaglutide plus Chinese brands ~80-150M units x $2-4 = $0.2-0.6B, plus development and tooling fees. 2030: generic semaglutide in loss-of-exclusivity (LOE) markets, 10-25M patient-years x 13 pens x $1.5-3 = $0.2-1.0B; next-wave innovators, 1.5-5M patient-years x 13-52 units x $3-6 = $0.1-1.0B (fewer units if dosing is monthly); other generics ~$0.1B -> total $0.8-1.8B. catalyst_timing: LOE in China/India/Brazil/Canada in 2026 (generic pen launches 2026-27); next-wave launches 2027-29; US/EU semaglutide LOE ~2031-32 drives device validation and stocking in 2029-30; new Ypsomed and SHL plants ramp 2026-28.
key_suppliers: Ypsomed (YPSN.SW, Switzerland/Germany; est. 30-40% of outsourced incretin pens/autoinjectors); SHL Medical (private, Switzerland/Taiwan/US; est. 20-30%, autoinjectors); Haselmeier (part of medmix, MEDX.SW; pens); Owen Mumford (private, UK); Nemera (private, France); Stevanato (STVN; Alina/Aidaptus); BD (BDX); Chinese domestic pen makers for local generics (names and shares unverified). supply_tightness: Moderate. Developing a platform device, completing human-factors work and filing it as a combination product takes 2-4 years. substitution_risk: High. Oral GLP-1s (orforglipron, oral Wegovy), vials in the cash-pay direct-to-consumer channel (Lilly Zepbound vials) and monthly dosing (MariTide, Metsera) cut device units by up to 4x. Generic makers in China and India may use in-house or low-cost local pens.
cyclicality_risk: Medium. Generic launches bring over-ordering and price wars (10+ entrants per market), so device orders swing and ASPs come under pressure.
faster_sub_niche: Multi-dose pens for generic semaglutide in the 2026 LOE markets grow fastest in 2026-28 (30-50% unit growth); autoinjectors for next-wave innovators lead in 2028-30. Captive pens grow ~5-12% and are excluded.

name: North American & European new-build sintered NdFeB magnets (DFARS-compliant, non-China inputs)
definition: IN: sintered NdFeB permanent magnets, including grain-boundary-diffused Dy/Tb grades, made in new plants in the US, Canada and EU from non-Chinese oxide/metal. Sold to defense primes, automotive Tier-1s, consumer electronics (Apple), robotics and industrial motors. Plants: MP Materials Independence (Fort Worth) and 10X; eVAC Sumter SC; Noveon (TX); USA Rare Earth Stillwater OK; Vulcan Elements; Neo Performance Narva (Estonia); other EU new-builds. OUT: Japanese incumbent output (Shin-Etsu, Proterial, TDK), which is split out as a slower sub-segment; Chinese-owned plants abroad; bonded NdFeB; SmCo; motor assembly; Indian new-build (separate policy-driven programme).
value_chain_path: Reshoring & critical minerals -> Rare-earth permanent-magnet supply chain -> Magnet manufacturing -> Sintered NdFeB -> North American/EU new-build, DFARS-compliant sintered NdFeB (incl. GBD high-coercivity grades)
also_serves_megatrends: AI data centers (HDD voice-coil motors, cooling pumps/fans)
size_2026_usd: $0.15-0.45B (own estimate: ~1.5-4 kt output x $80-120/kg)
volume_vs_price: About 95%+ of growth is volume. Output rises ~5-8x as MP 10X (2028), Vulcan, USAR Phase 2 and Neo Narva Phase 2 ramp. ASP is flat to -2-4%/yr because the ex-China premium (roughly 2x Chinese export prices; own estimate) narrows with scale. It cannot fall to Chinese levels while the input floor holds: NdPr oxide at the DoD $110/kg floor, plus ex-China Dy/Tb. The growth is durable mainly where offtake contracts exist: DoD buys 100% of 10X output for 10 years, plus Apple and GM. Uncontracted capacity faces real price risk.
math: 2030 top-down: announced NA+EU nameplate ~25-35 kt (MP ~10 kt total = Independence ~1-3 kt + 10X ~7 kt; Vulcan 10 kt; USAR ~4.8 kt with later ambition ~10 kt; eVAC ~1.5 kt; Noveon ~2 kt; Neo Narva 2 kt -> 5 kt). At 40-70% utilization by 2030 that gives ~10-25 kt. ASP build-up ($70-115/kg): NdPr ~30% by mass at $110-140/kg as metal = $35-42/kg; Dy/Tb (GBD, 0.5-2%) at ex-China $500-3,000/kg = $5-25/kg; Fe/B/Co ~$3-5/kg; conversion plus 20-30% yield loss = $25-45/kg. Revenue = $0.7-2.9B. 2026 bottom-up: MP 0.3-1 kt, eVAC 0.5-1 kt, Noveon 0.2-0.5 kt, USAR 0.1-0.4 kt, Neo 0.3-1 kt = ~1.5-4 kt x $80-120/kg = $0.12-0.48B. Demand check (own estimate), compliant demand in 2030: US ~6-15 kt (US-built EV/hybrid traction 2-7 kt at 1-2 kg/vehicle; defense 0.5-1.5 kt; consumer 0.5-1 kt; industrial, robots and fans 1-4 kt) plus EU ~3-8 kt. If every plant is built, supply could exceed compliant demand by 2029-30 unless the surplus is exported to Japanese/Korean OEMs. That caps the upper end.
catalyst_timing: Q4-2025: DoD NdPr price floor starts. 2026: MP Independence commercial ramp (GM first) and USAR Stillwater Phase 1 commissioning. Mid-2027: Apple recycled-feed magnets from Fort Worth. 1 Jan 2027: DFARS/10 USC 4872 bans China/Russia/NK/Iran content at any stage (mining, separation, production) in DoD magnets. ~10 Nov 2026: China's one-year suspension of its Oct-2025 export-control expansion expires, so re-escalation could raise ex-China demand. 2028: MP 10X commissioning. 2027-29: Vulcan 10 kt and USAR expansions; Neo Narva Phase 2.
key_suppliers: MP Materials (NYSE: MP; est. 30-45% of 2030 NA+EU new-build output); Vulcan Elements (private, US-government-backed; 10-25%); USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR, owns Less Common Metals UK; 10-20%); eVAC Magnetics (VAC Group, private/Ara Partners; 5-10%); Neo Performance Materials (TSX: NEO, Narva; 8-15%); Noveon Magnetics (private, recycled feed; 3-8%); Arnold Magnetic (private, small). Japan incumbents outside scope: Shin-Etsu (4063.T), Proterial (private/Bain), TDK (6762.T). Korea: Star Group (private); POSCO International (047050.KS) with ReElement on a US plant (MOU). supply_tightness: High. EV traction qualification (PPAP) takes ~18-36 months, and defense needs a documented mine-to-magnet chain. Process know-how is scarce outside China and Japan, even though the core Proterial patents have expired. Key equipment (strip casters, jet mills, sintering furnaces) has historically come from China or Japan, and China banned export of RE extraction/separation and magnet technology (Dec 2023 catalogue). A 1-10 kt plant takes 2-4 years to build. Ex-China Dy/Tb for GBD grades is the binding input (see C2). Pricing power is real only under offtake contracts.
substitution_risk: Medium. RE-free motors: BMW EESM, Renault wound-rotor, Tesla's stated plan for an RE-free PM motor (not yet shipped at scale). Ferrite and iron-nitride magnets (Niron) for lower-performance uses after 2028. Lower HRE content via GBD and Dy-free grades. The biggest threat is cheaper Chinese magnets (~$35-60/kg; own estimate) for commercial buyers if export licensing normalises. Defense demand cannot substitute after 2027.
cyclicality_risk: High on the overbuild side. US nameplate announced after the 2025 deals (~30+ kt) exceeds US compliant demand (~6-15 kt by 2030, own estimate). China can cut prices to strand Western plants, as it did with NdPr in 2023-24. Double ordering and stockpiling by OEMs in 2025-26 after the April-2025 controls inflates near-term orders. Mitigants: DoD 10X offtake and floor, Apple prepayment, government equity in Vulcan and USAR.
faster_sub_niche: The US-made, offtake-backed portion (MP Independence/10X, Vulcan, USAR) is faster: ~$0.1-0.3B (2026) -> $0.6-2.2B (2030), roughly 50-100% CAGR, because DFARS 2027 and DoD/Apple offtakes create captive demand. The EU (Neo Narva 2 -> 5 kt) grows more slowly. Japanese incumbents (~$1-2B, ~3-8% CAGR; own estimate) are excluded. Humanoid-robot magnet demand is too early to change the 2030 story.

name: Ex-China separated heavy rare earths: dysprosium & terbium oxide/metal
definition: IN: separated Dy and Tb oxides, and Dy/Tb metal or DyFe/TbFe/TbCu alloys used for grain-boundary diffusion, produced by non-Chinese separators from any feed (xenotime/monazite, ionic-clay concentrate, recycled magnets). Separators: Lynas Malaysia HRE circuit, Energy Fuels White Mesa, MP Mountain Pass HRE circuit, Iluka Eneabba, Solvay La Rochelle, Carester/Caremag (France), USAR, ReElement, Ucore, Aclara. OUT: mixed carbonate/concentrate sales; Chinese or Myanmar-origin supply, including Chinese-processed material re-exported; other heavies (Sm, Gd, Y, Lu), which are smaller and split out.
value_chain_path: Reshoring & critical minerals -> Rare earths -> Separation -> Heavy rare earths -> Ex-China separated Dy/Tb oxide & metal (GBD feedstock for high-coercivity NdFeB)
size_2026_usd: $40-200M (own estimate: ~40-150 t Dy+Tb oxide x blended $800-1,600/kg). The low end is borderline emerging.
cagr_2026_2030: 40-90% (very wide; depends on the price premium) (own estimate)
volume_vs_price: Volume grows ~8-12x as Lynas expands and Iluka (2027), MP's HRE circuit, Energy Fuels Phase 2 and Caremag start. Blended ASP falls ~30-55% cumulatively as the 2025 ex-China premium (~3-4x Chinese domestic) narrows to ~1.5-2x. More than 100% of revenue growth is volume, partly offset by price. The current revenue level is shortage-priced and fragile. The volume leg is durable because DFARS 2027 and OEM dual-sourcing need non-Chinese Dy/Tb for every compliant GBD magnet.
math: Demand (own estimate): ex-China magnet output in 2030 of ~35-60 kt (Japan incumbents ~15-25 kt + C1 new-build 10-25 kt + India/Korea 2-6 kt) x Dy+Tb ~1.2-3% of magnet mass = ~420-1,800 t metal ~ 480-2,100 t oxide. Supply 2026 (own estimate): Lynas 30-120 t, Energy Fuels <10 t, Solvay <20 t, others ~0, total ~40-150 t. Price: Dy ~$600-900/kg and Tb ~$2,500-4,000/kg ex-China; at ~75:25 Dy:Tb by mass, blended ~$800-1,600/kg. Revenue $32-240M -> $40-200M. Supply 2030 (own estimate): Lynas 150-400 t, Iluka 100-300 t, Carester 100-300 t (incl. recycled), Energy Fuels 50-250 t, MP 50-200 t, others (USAR, Aclara, ReElement, Ucore, Solvay, Neo) 50-200 t, total ~500-1,500 t. Price: Dy $350-600/kg and Tb $1,000-2,500/kg, blended $450-1,100/kg. Revenue $0.23-1.65B -> $0.3-1.4B.
catalyst_timing: 2025: Lynas produced its first ex-China Dy (May) and Tb (June). 2026: Lynas expands its Malaysia HRE circuit; MP's Mountain Pass HRE circuit (DoD $150M loan) targets ~mid-2026; Caremag start-up 2026-27. ~10 Nov 2026: China's control suspension expires (renewal or escalation). 1 Jan 2027: DFARS full-chain ban. 2027: Iluka Eneabba commissioning. 2027-28: Energy Fuels Phase 2. 2028+: Aclara (Louisiana) and ionic-clay feed from Brazil.
key_suppliers: 2026 (own estimates): Lynas Rare Earths (ASX: LYC) ~60-85% of ex-China separated Dy/Tb; Energy Fuels (NYSE American: UUUU / TSX: EFR) <10%; Solvay (EBR: SOLB, La Rochelle) <10%. 2030 (own estimates): Lynas 25-35%; Iluka (ASX: ILU) 10-20%; Carester/Caremag (private, backed by JOGMEC/Iwatani) 10-20%; MP Materials (NYSE: MP) 5-15%; Energy Fuels 5-15%; USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR), Aclara (TSX: ARA), ReElement (private), Ucore (TSXV: UCU) and Neo (TSX: NEO) 10-20% combined. HRE-rich feed: Serra Verde (Brazil, private, US DFC-backed), Lynas Mt Weld, Iluka stockpile, Malaysian ionic clay.
supply_tightness: Extreme. Heavy-RE separation needs very long SX cascades or chromatography. China holds ~99% of HRE separation (IEA-type estimates) and bans export of separation technology. HRE-rich feed is scarce outside China and Myanmar; Mountain Pass bastnaesite is HRE-poor. Magnet makers take ~6-12 months to qualify oxide/metal purity for GBD. New circuits take 2-4 years. Pricing power is high now but depends on Chinese licensing policy.
substitution_risk: Medium. GBD has already cut Dy per magnet ~50-80% versus bulk alloying, and further thrift continues (Dy-free grades from Daido/Honda and Toyota; Ce substitution). RE-free motors cut the whole magnet. The largest 'substitute' is normalised Chinese supply: general licences would pull Western prices back toward Chinese levels.
cyclicality_risk: High. Japanese, Korean and Western buyers stockpiled and double-ordered in 2025-26 after the April-2025 controls, inflating ex-China prices. Premium collapse is possible if China grants general licences after Nov 2026. Overbuild is possible by 2029-30 if Lynas, Iluka, Caremag, MP, Energy Fuels and Aclara all deliver at once.
faster_sub_niche: Terbium may grow faster in value than Dy: higher $/kg, more coercivity per gram, preferred in GBD for high-temperature EV and defense grades. The split could not be verified this session, so none is confirmed.

name: Non-FEOC graphite anode active material (AAM) for US/allied cell plants
definition: IN: battery-grade coated spherical natural graphite and synthetic graphite AAM from producers that are not 'prohibited foreign entities' under OBBBA. They are located in North America, Korea, Japan, Europe and India and supply cell makers serving the US (EV + stationary storage) and EU. Producers: POSCO Future M, Japanese producers, Syrah Vidalia, Novonix, Vianode, NMG, Talga, Epsilon, Westwater. OUT: Chinese AAM, including Chinese-owned plants in Morocco and Indonesia (FEOC); unprocessed flake concentrate; silicon anodes; hard carbon; stand-alone needle-coke or graphitization tolling.
value_chain_path: Reshoring & critical minerals -> Battery minerals (non-FEOC) -> Graphite -> Anode active material -> Non-FEOC AAM (fastest: North American synthetic-graphite AAM)
also_serves_megatrends: Grid & AI-data-center battery energy storage (LFP ESS)
size_2026_usd: $0.8-1.5B (own estimate: ~100-160 kt x $7-10/kg)
volume_vs_price: About 100% of growth is volume (~3x tonnes). ASP is flat to slightly down. The non-FEOC premium (~1.5-2.5x over Chinese ~$3-5/kg; own estimate) is held up by policy: AD/CVD, Sec. 301 and the 45X material-assistance cost ratio. It erodes slowly as Western scale arrives. This is the most durable growth in this driver because regulation forces the volume, rather than shortage pricing driving it.
math: 2026 bottom-up (own estimate) of non-FEOC AAM shipments: POSCO Future M ~40-70 kt (capacity ~80+ kt natural + ~8 kt synthetic, low utilization); Japanese producers (Resonac, Mitsubishi Chemical, Nippon Carbon, JFE Chemical) ~30-50 kt; Syrah Vidalia ~<5-10 kt; Novonix 0-3 kt; Europe/India 5-15 kt. Total ~90-150 kt x $7-10/kg = $0.6-1.5B. 2030 top-down (own estimate): US cell output ~300-450 GWh (EV 150-250 + ESS 100-200) x ~1.0-1.1 kg graphite/kWh = 300-500 kt AAM demand. With the 45X MACR for battery components rising to ~85% by 2030 and AD/CVD on Chinese AAM, 50-80% would be non-FEOC, i.e. 150-400 kt. Add EU/Japan/Korea non-FEOC demand for US-bound and EU-localised cells (~100-150 kt), giving ~300-500 kt x $6.5-9/kg = $2.0-4.5B.
catalyst_timing: Jul 2025: preliminary US AD duty (~93.5%) on Chinese active anode material; final AD/CVD orders due early 2026 (outcome unverified this session). 1 Jan 2026: Sec. 301 tariff increases on Chinese natural graphite and non-EV Li-ion batteries. 2026-2030: 45X/48E prohibited-foreign-entity rules, with the battery-component threshold stepping up each year. 2026: Novonix Chattanooga first commercial output (guidance). 2027: Vianode's North American plant (GM supply). 2027-28: NMG Becancour. 2026-28: US LFP ESS cell plant ramps (LGES Michigan, Ford Kentucky ESS conversion, Samsung SDI/SK On ESS lines).
key_suppliers: POSCO Future M (KRX: 003670; est. 30-45% of 2026 non-FEOC AAM); Japanese producers: Resonac (4004.T), Mitsubishi Chemical (4188.T), Nippon Carbon (5302.T), JFE Chemical (JFE 5411.T); ~25-35% combined. Syrah Resources (ASX: SYR, Vidalia LA; <5%); Novonix (ASX/Nasdaq: NVX, Chattanooga TN; <3% in 2026, rising); Vianode (private: Hydro/Elkem/Altor; Norway + Canada); Nouveau Monde Graphite (TSXV/NYSE: NMG); Talga (ASX: TLG, Sweden); Epsilon Advanced Materials (private, India + North Carolina); Westwater (NYSE American: WWR, stalled); Graphite One (TSXV: GPH, Ohio plan). All shares are own estimates.
supply_tightness: High for qualified non-FEOC supply. Cell-maker qualification takes ~18-36 months; Syrah's multi-year Vidalia qualification struggle and Tesla's 2025 default notice show this. Graphitization furnace capacity and needle coke are bottlenecks. China holds ~90%+ of AAM and >95% of spheroidization. China licenses graphite exports (Dec 2023) and in Oct 2025 extended controls to anode technology and equipment (suspended to Nov 2026). Plant builds take 2-4 years. Chinese AAM plants run at ~50% utilization, so global prices stay low and only the policy-protected segment has pricing power.
substitution_risk: Medium-low through 2030. Silicon-carbon blends (5-15% Si) trim graphite per kWh by ~5-15%. Sodium-ion with hard carbon could take ESS share after 2028. LFP-to-LMFP is neutral. The main competitive leak is Chinese material routed through non-FEOC-owned third-country processors.
cyclicality_risk: Medium-high. US EV demand reset after the 30D credit ended (30 Sept 2025), with OEM write-downs and cancelled EV programmes. ESS (AI data centers + grid) is the swing demand. Project delays (Syrah, Westwater), policy reversal risk, and Chinese overcapacity holding the global price ~$3-5/kg.
faster_sub_niche: North American synthetic-graphite AAM (Novonix, Vianode Canada, Epsilon NC, others): ~5-20 kt (~$50-180M) in 2026 -> ~60-130 kt (~$0.45-1.1B) in 2030, ~50-90% CAGR (own estimate). It is faster because LFP ESS cells (now the main US growth) prefer synthetic graphite and because of the 45X MACR. It also carries higher execution risk.

name: Ex-China NdPr oxide and NdPr metal/alloy (light rare-earth separation + metallization)
definition: IN: separated NdPr oxide and NdPr metal (plus NdFeB master alloy) produced outside the China/Myanmar supply chain, both merchant sales and captive transfers. Separators: Lynas (Malaysia, Kalgoorlie), MP Mountain Pass, Solvay La Rochelle, Neo Silmet, Energy Fuels, Iluka (2027), Arafura (2028+). Metallization: MP Independence, Less Common Metals (USAR), KSM Metals (Korea), Japanese captive metal makers. OUT: concentrate and mixed carbonate; Ce/La products; Chinese-tolled material; finished magnets (C1); heavies (C2).
value_chain_path: Reshoring & critical minerals -> Rare earths -> Separation & metallization -> Light rare earths (NdPr) -> Ex-China NdPr oxide + NdPr metal/alloy
size_2026_usd: $0.9-1.7B (own estimate: ~11-16 kt NdPr oxide-equivalent x blended $85-105/kg)
volume_vs_price: About 75-85% of growth is volume (~2-2.5x tonnes) and 15-25% price. Blended ASP rises ~0-6%/yr: the DoD $110/kg floor applies to MP, Lynas is linked to the Chinese price plus a provenance premium, and Project Vault/stockpile buying sets a floor. The price leg is policy-anchored, not a pure shortage. The volume leg depends on Lynas reaching ~12 kt/yr, MP Stage II/10X feed, Iluka 2027 and Energy Fuels Phase 2.
math: 2026 bottom-up (own estimate): Lynas ~7-10 kt (target capacity ~10.5-12 kt/yr); MP ~3-4.5 kt (Q3-2025 record ~721 t/quarter, so a run-rate of ~2.9 kt/yr before growth); Solvay, Neo, Energy Fuels and others ~0.5-1.5 kt. Total ~11-16 kt x $85-105/kg (Lynas ~China price $78-98/kg + premium; MP at the $110 floor) = $0.94-1.68B. 2030 (own estimate): Lynas 12-15 kt, MP 6-10 kt, Iluka 3-4 kt, Energy Fuels 2-6 kt, Arafura 1-4 kt, Solvay/Neo/Carester 2-4 kt, others (USAR, Aclara, Saudi Maaden-MP, Kazakhstan) 1-4 kt. Total 27-47 kt, haircut to 25-40 kt for delays, x $90-125/kg = $2.25-5.0B. Captive transfers (MP oxide to MP magnets) are included at market value.
catalyst_timing: Q4-2025: MP $110/kg floor payments begin. 2026: Lynas at full ~12 kt/yr target (guidance); USAR closes the LCM acquisition and expands metal output. Feb 2026: Project Vault civilian reserve and allied price-floor discussions. 2027: Iluka Eneabba. 2027-28: Energy Fuels Phase 2. 2028: MP 10X pulls in all MP oxide. 2028-29: Arafura Nolans. ~Nov 2026: China control renewal decision.
key_suppliers: Separation (own estimates of 2026 ex-China share): Lynas Rare Earths (ASX: LYC) ~55-65%; MP Materials (NYSE: MP) ~20-30%; Solvay (EBR: SOLB), Neo Performance/Silmet (TSX: NEO) and Energy Fuels (NYSE American: UUUU) ~5-10% combined. Later entrants: Iluka (ASX: ILU), Arafura (ASX: ARU). Metallization: Less Common Metals (owned by USA Rare Earth, Nasdaq: USAR); KSM Metals (Korea, private); Santoku and Shin-Etsu captive (Japan); MP Independence captive.
supply_tightness: High at separation and very high at metallization. Ex-China oxide-to-metal capacity is only a few kt/yr (own estimate), while C1 plus Indian and Korean magnet plants need ~8-15 kt/yr of metal by 2030. Molten-salt electrolysis cells and know-how are concentrated in China, and China bans export of the technology. New SX plants take 2-4 years; qualifying metal/alloy at magnet makers takes ~6-12 months.
substitution_risk: Low-medium. Recycled NdPr (swarf and EOL), plus the motor substitution risks listed under C1. The main risk is Chinese NdPr price competition for uncontracted volumes.
cyclicality_risk: Medium-high. NdPr has a history of boom-bust (2022 peak ~$150/kg -> 2024 ~$55-60/kg). Chinese quota policy can swing the price. The MP floor protects only MP. If ex-China magnet plants (C1) are delayed, oxide could end up with no ex-China home and be sold at Chinese prices.
faster_sub_niche: Merchant ex-China RE metal/alloy conversion (LCM/USAR, KSM Metals, new US/Korean electrolysis lines): ~$0.1-0.3B (2026) -> ~$0.6-1.5B (2030), ~45-70% CAGR (own estimate). It is faster because ex-China magnet capacity is growing far faster than ex-China metallization. Not separately verifiable this session.

name: Ex-China germanium: refined Ge, GeCl4, Ge blanks and substrates
definition: IN: germanium refined and converted outside China, i.e. GeO2, GeCl4 for fiber preforms, Ge metal and ingot, IR optical blanks, and Ge wafers for III-V space solar cells. Producers: Umicore (Olen), Teck Trail, 5N Plus/AZUR SPACE, Korea Zinc, Nyrstar/US plans, and Umicore's processing of Gécamines/STL (DRC) tailings. OUT: Chinese-refined Ge, including Chinese-made substrates (e.g. AXT's China operations); downstream lenses, cameras and solar cells; Russian supply (JSC Germanium).
value_chain_path: Reshoring & critical minerals -> Export-controlled minor metals -> Germanium -> Refining & first-stage products (GeCl4, Ge metal, blanks, substrates) -> Ex-China supply (fastest: Ge substrates for space III-V solar)
size_2026_usd: $0.15-0.6B (own estimate: ~40-70 t refined Ge-equivalent x $3,000-5,500/kg metal value x 1.0-1.5 first-stage value-add)
volume_vs_price: Mixed. Volume grows ~1.5-2x from new by-product recovery (DRC Big Hill tailings, Korea Zinc US smelter ~2029, Teck/Nyrstar options). Price is likely flat to down from 2025-26 export-control highs (ex-China ~1.5-2.5x the Chinese price; own estimate). A large share of the 2026 revenue level is shortage pricing, so the growth is less durable than in C1 or C3.
math: Own estimate. 2026: ex-China refined Ge-equivalent ~40-70 t (Umicore ~25-40 t including recycling, Teck ~10-20 t, others ~5-10 t) x $3,000-5,500/kg = $120-385M metal value, x1.0-1.5 for GeCl4, blank and substrate conversion = $0.12-0.58B. 2030: 70-120 t x $2,500-5,000/kg x 1.0-1.5 = $0.18-0.9B. Space-solar substrate sub-niche: space III-V solar cell market of ~$0.5-1.0B with the Ge substrate share at ~15-25% gives ~$0.1-0.25B (2026). Growing with LEO constellation and SDA tranche builds, that reaches ~$0.25-0.55B (2030), unverified.
catalyst_timing: ~27 Nov 2026: China's suspension of its US-specific Ga/Ge/Sb export ban (MOFCOM No.46) expires; August-2023 licensing persists. 2026-28: SDA PWSA tranche launches, Amazon Kuiper deployment and EU IRIS2 procurement. 2026-28: AI data-center fiber build-out. ~2029: Korea Zinc US (Tennessee) smelter adds Ge/Ga/Sb/In by-product output. Ongoing: Ukraine/European drone thermal-optics demand.
key_suppliers: Umicore (EBR: UMI; est. 40-55% of ex-China refined Ge); Teck Resources (NYSE: TECK, Trail BC; 15-25%); 5N Plus (TSX: VNP, owns AZUR SPACE, leading ex-China space Ge substrates; with Umicore likely >70% of ex-China space-grade substrates); Korea Zinc (KRX: 010130; Onsan, plus planned US smelter); Nyrstar (Trafigura, Clarksville TN Ge/Ga project); Gécamines/STL (DRC feed to Umicore). All shares are own estimates.
supply_tightness: High at the primary end: Ge is a by-product, so supply cannot respond to price without a zinc/coal-ash host. China holds ~60-70%+ of refinery output. Space-grade substrate qualification is long (~2-3 years with cell makers such as Spectrolab, Rocket Lab/SolAero and AZUR). IR-grade blanks are qualified by defense primes.
substitution_risk: Medium-high. Chalcogenide glasses replace Ge lenses in uncooled LWIR. Starlink-type LEO buses use silicon cells rather than III-V-on-Ge. Recycling of fiber and optics scrap (Umicore) caps primary demand.
cyclicality_risk: High. Export-control-driven price spikes invite recycling, thrift and Chinese re-entry once licences ease. Defense and space demand is lumpy, programme by programme.
faster_sub_niche: Ge substrates (wafers) for III-V multijunction space solar cells: ~$0.1-0.25B (2026) -> ~$0.25-0.55B (2030), ~15-30% CAGR (own estimate, unverified). Driven by LEO/defense constellations, but Starlink's silicon choice limits the upside.

name: Transcatheter tricuspid & mitral valve REPLACEMENT systems (TTVR + TMVR)
definition: IN: catheter-delivered replacement heart valves and their delivery systems for the tricuspid position (Edwards EVOQUE, Jenscare LuX-Valve Plus, Medtronic Intrepid TTVR, VDyne) and the mitral position (Edwards SAPIEN M3 transseptal TMVR, Abbott Tendyne, Medtronic Intrepid). OUT: edge-to-edge repair clips (MitraClip, PASCAL, TriClip), TAVR, surgical valves, annuloplasty.
value_chain_path: Healthcare -> cardiovascular devices -> structural heart -> transcatheter mitral/tricuspid therapies (TMTT) -> transcatheter valve replacement (TTVR + TMVR) systems
also_serves_megatrends: Population aging (tricuspid regurgitation prevalence rises steeply after 75)
Shift from open surgery to catheter procedures and shorter stays
size_2026_usd: $0.35-0.6B (own estimate built from Edwards TMTT guidance; replacement assumed ~55-70% of Edwards TMTT plus Abbott/China)
size_2030_usd: $1.4-2.6B (own estimate; Edwards' ~$2B 2030 TMTT aspiration covers repair plus replacement)
volume_vs_price: About 90% volume: new implanting centers, CMS national coverage (with registry), EU rollout, first full years of TMVR. ASP is flat to slightly up: premium devices around $40-50k US (own estimate, unverified), with no competing approved US TTVR to force price cuts before ~2028. Price is not shortage-driven, so the growth is durable.
math: 2026 top-down: EVOQUE ~6-9k implants x $38-48k = $0.23-0.43B; SAPIEN M3 first full year ~1-2k x $42-50k = $0.04-0.10B; Tendyne + China LuX-Valve + others ~$0.03-0.08B. Total $0.30-0.61B. 2030: TTVR 25-40k implants (US+EU+China) x $36-45k = $0.9-1.8B; TMVR 10-18k x $40-48k = $0.4-0.86B. Total $1.3-2.66B. Cross-check: Edwards guided TMTT (repair+replacement) ~$500-530M for 2025 and stated ~$2B by 2030; adding Abbott Tendyne/TriClip-adjacent replacement and China implies a replacement-only 2030 range of $1.4-2.6B. All unit counts and ASPs are own estimates.
catalyst_timing: EVOQUE FDA approval Feb-2024. CMS NCDs for T-TEER and TTVR finalized 2025, opening Medicare coverage. SAPIEN M3 CE mark Apr-2025; US approval reported late 2025 (unverified). Abbott Tendyne FDA approval May-2025. Medtronic Intrepid pivotal data ~2026-27 (unverified). China NMPA approvals (Jenscare LuX-Valve Plus) 2026-27 (unverified). EU and Japan reimbursement 2026-2028.
key_suppliers: Edwards Lifesciences (EW, NYSE, US): ~70-85% of 2026 replacement revenue (EVOQUE, SAPIEN M3). Abbott (ABT, NYSE): Tendyne, ~5-10%. Medtronic (MDT, NYSE): Intrepid, pre-commercial. Jenscare Scientific (9877.HK, China): LuX-Valve, China and US trials (TRAVEL II). Peijia Medical (9996.HK), MicroPort CardioFlow (2160.HK): China pipelines. VDyne and Innovalve (private). Shares are own estimates.
supply_tightness: Manufacturing is not the bottleneck; regulation and clinical adoption are. Entry needs a PMA backed by randomized trials (5-8 years). Only 1-2 approved products per position. Throughput is limited by trained implanters, TEE/CT imaging and CED registry requirements. This gives incumbents strong pricing power, and competition before ~2028 is limited to Abbott (mitral) and Medtronic (pending).
substitution_risk: Medium. TEER repair is cheaper and less invasive for suitable anatomy, and cannibalizes the moderate-TR segment. New-pacemaker rates after TTVR (~15-25% in trials) and bleeding/anticoagulation burden could limit expansion into less sick patients. Long-term durability data is still pending.
cyclicality_risk: Low. Procedure-driven with no capex cycle and no Chinese overcapacity (China players are domestic-focused). Risks are a safety signal, coding/DRG changes, and the FTC's challenge to Edwards' structural-heart M&A (JenaValve) as a sign of antitrust scrutiny.
faster_sub_niche: TMVR (SAPIEN M3, Tendyne, Intrepid) is the faster sub-segment: ~$0.04-0.12B in 2026 to $0.4-0.86B in 2030 (55-90% CAGR), but with lower confidence and a smaller base. TTVR (EVOQUE) is the larger, more certain engine. TEER repair (~10-15% CAGR) was split out and dropped.
