name: Non-carrier-added lutetium-177 (n.c.a. Lu-177) isotope supply
definition: IN: GMP-grade non-carrier-added Lu-177 chloride, made by irradiating enriched Yb-176 targets in research reactors and then separating Lu from Yb radiochemically. Sold to radiopharma companies or produced in-house, valued at merchant or transfer price. OUT: carrier-added Lu-177 (Lu-176 route), finished drug revenue (Pluvicto, Lutathera, ITM-11), targeting ligands, alpha emitters (Ac-225, Pb-212), diagnostic isotopes.
value_chain_path: Healthcare -> oncology therapeutics -> radioligand therapy (RLT) -> therapeutic isotope supply -> beta emitters -> n.c.a. Lu-177 (Yb-176 route)
also_serves_megatrends: Nuclear industrial base (research reactors, SMR/CANDU isotope production, stable-isotope enrichment shared with nuclear fuel and quantum materials)
size_2026_usd: $0.23-0.55B (own estimate; merchant plus captive transfer value)
volume_vs_price: Dose volume +30-45%/yr from label expansions into earlier lines, new Lu-177 agents and ex-US rollout. Price per GBq -5 to -10%/yr as SHINE, ITM, Eckert & Ziegler, NRG/Curium and Chinese CANDU output ramp. Roughly 80% of revenue growth is volume, so it is durable, but price will deflate.
math: 2026 dose model: Pluvicto ~$2.3-2.8B / blended $35-45k per dose = ~55-75k doses. Lutathera ~$0.8-1.0B / $40-50k = ~17-25k doses. Clinical-trial and other commercial doses (ITM-11 launch, Curium Lu-PSMA-I&T, China/India) ~15-30k. Total ~90-130k dose-equivalents. Each 7.4 GBq dose at calibration needs roughly 1.5-2.5x that activity at end of processing. Isotope value ~$2.5-4.5k per dose-equivalent gives $0.23-0.58B. 2030: 300-500k doses (Pluvicto in mHSPC and pre-taxane lines, Lutathera 1L, ITM-11, Lu-PSMA-I&T, 5-10 newer Lu-177 ligands, China) x $2.0-3.5k = $0.6-1.75B. Cross-check against FY2024 sales (Pluvicto $1.39B, Lutathera $0.72B) and FY2025 Pluvicto ~$1.9-2.0B (unverified). Isotope value per dose is my estimate and unverified; it is the biggest swing factor.
catalyst_timing: Pluvicto pre-taxane mCRPC label (PSMAfore), FDA Mar-2025. Pluvicto mHSPC (PSMAddition) filing 2H-2025, US decision 2026 (unverified). ITM-11 (n.c.a. Lu-177 edotreotide; COMPETE positive Jan-2025) NDA under review, US decision ~2026 (unverified). Curium Lu-PSMA-I&T (ECLIPSE) NDA. Novartis new RLT plants (Carlsbad CA; Florida and Texas announced Apr-2025). Pallas reactor (NL) ~2030 replacing HFR Petten. FRM II (Munich) return to service.
key_suppliers: ITM Isotope Technologies Munich (private, DE): largest merchant n.c.a. supplier, est. 30-45% (own estimate). SHINE Technologies (private, US, Janesville WI): est. 10-20%. Eckert & Ziegler (EUZ, Xetra, DE): est. 5-15%. NRG/Curium (private, NL/FR). Novartis (NOVN, SIX): captive processing plus long-term offtake. ANSTO (AU gov), NTP/SAFARI-1 (ZA), Isotopia (IL), KAERI/HANARO (KR). China: China Isotope & Radiation (1763.HK, CNNC) incl. Qinshan CANDU production (unverified), Dongcheng Pharma (002675.SZ). Yb-176 enrichment: Rosatom/JSC Isotope (RU), Urenco Stable Isotopes (NL/UK), ASP Isotopes (ASPI, Nasdaq; laser enrichment in South Africa), US DOE Isotope Program/ORNL. All shares are unverified own estimates.
supply_tightness: Three stacked bottlenecks. (1) Enriched Yb-176 (>99%) has historically been concentrated in Russia; Urenco and laser enrichment (ASPI) are ramping. (2) Irradiation slots in ~15-20 aging high-flux research reactors; unplanned outages at BR2, HFR and MURR have caused past shortages. (3) GMP hot-cell separation. Adding a new isotope source to a marketed NDA/MAA needs a prior-approval supplement (~9-18 months), so a qualified source is sticky. On the other side, announced capacity (ITM NOVA site in Garching, SHINE expansions, Chinese reactors) likely exceeds demand by ~2028-29, which argues for falling price per GBq.
substitution_risk: Medium after 2029. Alpha emitters (Ac-225, Pb-212) could displace Lu-177 in later lines once approved (~2028-30). Tb-161 (via Gd-160) is a next-generation beta emitter. Carrier-added Lu-177 is cheaper but leaves Lu-177m waste, so the market keeps shifting toward n.c.a.
cyclicality_risk: Demand is not cyclical. Supply risks: reactor outages (price spikes, not durable), sanctions on Russian Yb-176, and overbuild 2028+ as many isotope startups commission capacity at once.
faster_sub_niche: Split: enriched Yb-176 targets grow with dose count but are small (<$50-100M), and recycling of Yb-176 slows the growth in $ terms, so they are emerging and sub-scale. Carrier-added Lu-177 is shrinking. n.c.a. Lu-177 is the faster segment at investable scale. Finished-dose RLT CDMO/radiopharmacy grows at a similar rate but is fragmented.

name: ADC payload-linker HPAPI + bioconjugation drug-substance CDMO
definition: IN: outsourced GMP manufacture of ADC payload-linkers (high-potency, OEB4-5: Topo-I exatecan/DXd-class, MMAE/MMAF, novel dual-payload) and the antibody-payload conjugation step (drug substance), plus cytotoxic fill/finish, including clinical and commercial supply. OUT: naked mAb intermediate made in standard CHO capacity when billed separately; innovators' in-house capacity (Daiichi Sankyo, Pfizer/Seagen, AstraZeneca); ADC drug sales.
value_chain_path: Healthcare -> oncology biologics -> antibody-drug conjugates -> CMC outsourcing -> payload-linker HPAPI synthesis + bioconjugation drug substance (CDMO)
also_serves_megatrends: China biotech out-licensing boom (a large share of global ADC licensing deals originate in China)
Next-generation biologics (bispecific ADCs, dual-payload, degrader-antibody conjugates)
Pharma supply-chain reshoring/BIOSECURE (shifts share and capex geography)
size_2026_usd: $2.3-3.3B (own estimate, supplier bottom-up)
size_2030_usd: $5.5-9B (own estimate; third-party prospectus forecast ~$11B for broader ADC outsourcing incl. mAb)
volume_vs_price: ~85% volume: more commercial ADCs (Datroway, Emrelis, sac-TMT ex-China, Enhertu earlier-line labels) and a pipeline of hundreds of clinical ADCs. Price/mix is mildly positive because OEB5 capacity is scarce and payload chemistry is complex (20+ steps). Growth is not shortage-priced, so it is durable while capacity is being added.
math: Bottom-up 2026: WuXi XDC ~RMB 7.0-8.5B (~$1.0-1.2B; ~35-45% share). Lonza bioconjugates ~$0.35-0.6B (unverified, not separately disclosed). MilliporeSigma, Piramal, Abzena, Sterling, Ajinomoto Bio-Pharma, Axplora, BSP, Samsung Biologics and Chinese peers combined ~$0.9-1.5B. Total ~$2.3-3.3B. Top-down 2026: ADC drug sales ~$22-28B; payload/conjugation/fill COGS ~10-15% of sales = $2.2-4.2B, ~50-65% outsourced, plus clinical CMC services ~$0.8-1.2B, giving $1.9-3.9B. 2030: ADC sales $45-65B (third-party consensus range, unverified) at the same ratios gives $5.5-9B.
catalyst_timing: Enhertu earlier-line HER2+ labels (DESTINY-Breast09/05) 2026. Datroway lung labels 2025-26. Merck's sac-TMT global Phase 3 readouts 2026-27. 10-20 ADC BLAs expected 2026-2029. WuXi XDC Singapore site GMP start ~2026. BIOSECURE provisions (FY2026 NDAA, Dec-2025; implementation timing unverified) push Western sponsors to dual-source by ~2028-2032.
key_suppliers: WuXi XDC (2268.HK, China/Singapore): est. 35-45% of outsourced. Lonza (LONN, SIX; Visp + Synaffix linker tech): ~15-20%. MilliporeSigma (Merck KGaA, MRK.DE; St. Louis/Madison HPAPI): ~5-8%. Piramal Pharma Solutions (PPLPHARMA.NS; Grangemouth/Lexington): ~4-6%. Abzena (private): ~3-5%. Sterling Pharma Solutions (private, UK). Ajinomoto Bio-Pharma (2802.T; AJICAP). Axplora (private, payloads). BSP Pharmaceuticals (private, IT; fill/finish). Samsung Biologics (207940.KS; ADC suite opened ~2025). Porton (300363.SZ), Asymchem (002821.SZ). Shares are own estimates.
supply_tightness: Real but easing. OEB5 containment suites and payload synthesis expertise are limited. New capacity takes 24-36 months to build. Commercial tech transfer plus PPQ takes 12-24 months, so qualified suppliers are sticky. WuXi XDC has reported a fast-growing backlog (~US$1.3B mid-2025). Lonza, Samsung, Piramal, Sterling and Chinese peers are all adding suites, so expect tightness through 2027 and normalization after.
substitution_risk: Medium. Big pharma is reshoring in-house: Daiichi Sankyo is investing heavily in DXd and conjugation capacity in Japan, Germany and the US. Competing modalities (bispecific T-cell engagers, radioligands, in vivo CAR-T later) could take indications. Geopolitics moves share from China to the West without changing total size.
cyclicality_risk: Medium. Clinical-stage demand follows the biotech funding cycle (a 2022-23 slump). Chinese CDMO capacity could overbuild ~2028. A few blockbuster ADC failures or safety findings (ILD) could dent demand. Double ordering is limited because contracts are program-specific.
faster_sub_niche: Topo-I-class payload-linker HPAPI (exatecan/DXd derivatives, now most new ADC programs) and integrated 'one-stop' providers serving China-origin programs (WuXi XDC grew ~91% in 2024 and ~62% in H1-2025) likely grow 30-45%, versus ~20-25% for MMAE-era conjugation. Not separately disclosed, so I kept the integrated niche.

name: Large-scale oligonucleotide (siRNA/ASO) API manufacturing for cardiometabolic indications
definition: IN: commercial-scale (multi-kg to tonne) GMP synthesis, purification and isolation of siRNA and antisense drug substances for common cardiometabolic diseases (LDL-C/PCSK9, Lp(a), TG/APOC3, ATTR-cardiomyopathy, angiotensinogen/hypertension), plus dedicated raw materials (2'-F, 2'-OMe, MOE phosphoramidites; GalNAc ligand; solid supports). OUT: peptide/GLP-1 capacity (even when in the same 'TIDES' unit), research-scale oligos, mRNA, rare-disease clinical batches, DNA synthesis for genomics.
value_chain_path: Healthcare -> cardiometabolic therapeutics (ex-GLP-1) -> nucleic-acid therapeutics (siRNA/ASO) -> drug-substance manufacturing -> large-scale solid-phase oligo synthesis/purification (+ amidite & GalNAc inputs)
also_serves_megatrends: Cardiovascular prevention in aging populations (Lp(a), hypertension)
Neurology ASOs (ALS, Huntington, Alzheimer's tau programs)
Synthetic-chemistry tooling shared with DNA synthesis / synthetic biology
size_2026_usd: $1.5-2.6B (own estimate; all outsourced oligo API plus amidites; cardiometabolic is ~30-45% of it)
size_2030_usd: $3.5-6.5B (own estimate; heavily dependent on Lp(a)/CV outcome trial readouts)
volume_vs_price: Volume (kg) +40-70%/yr as oligos move from rare disease (grams per patient-year) to mass CV prevention (0.3-1 g per patient-year). Price per gram -10 to -20%/yr as batch scale moves to multi-mol and hybrid ligation/liquid-phase processes spread. Revenue growth is almost entirely volume, with real price deflation built in.
math: Content per patient-year: inclisiran 284 mg x2 = 0.57 g; pelacarsen 80 mg monthly = 0.96 g; olezarsen (sHTG) 80 mg monthly = ~0.96 g; olpasiran ~0.3 g; zilebesiran ~0.6-1.2 g; vutrisiran 0.1 g. 2026 common-disease patients on oligos ~1.0-1.8M, so ~0.5-1.2 t API. 2030 with at least one positive Lp(a) outcomes trial: 4-10M patients, so 3-8 t. CDMO pricing ~$300-800/g (2026) to ~$150-400/g (2030). CV API value: 2026 $0.15-0.9B, 2030 $0.6-3.0B. Bottom-up all-oligo 2026 (own estimates, unverified): Agilent NASD ~$0.35-0.5B; Nitto Avecia ~$0.4-0.6B; ST Pharm ~$0.25-0.35B; Bachem oligos ~$0.1-0.2B; WuXi STA oligo ex-peptide ~$0.2-0.4B; Sumitomo Chemical, Kaneka Eurogentec, Corden and others ~$0.1-0.25B; amidites (Hongene, Thermo, ChemGenes, Sigma) ~$0.15-0.35B. Total $1.55-2.65B.
catalyst_timing: Amvuttra ATTR-CM label (FDA Mar-2025) ramp. Ionis olezarsen sHTG approval ~2026 (unverified). Novartis/Ionis pelacarsen Lp(a)HORIZON CV outcomes readout 2026 (result unverified). Amgen olpasiran OCEAN(a)-Outcomes ~2026-27. Leqvio CV outcomes (ORION-4/V-VICTORION) ~2026-27. Arrowhead plozasiran sHTG Phase 3s ~2026-27. Lilly lepodisiran ACCLAIM-Lp(a) ~2029. Zilebesiran CVOT 2030+. Capacity: ST Pharm second oligo plant ~2026 (unverified); Agilent Frederick Train B/C online; Bachem Bubendorf expansion.
key_suppliers: Agilent Technologies (A, NYSE; Boulder/Frederick). Nitto Denko/Nitto Avecia (6988.T; US/JP). ST Pharm (237690.KQ, Korea). Bachem (BANB, SIX). WuXi STA / WuXi AppTec (603259.SS / 2359.HK). Sumitomo Chemical (4005.T). Kaneka Eurogentec (4118.T). Corden Pharma (private). Amidites/GalNAc: Hongene Biotech (private, China; widely cited as the largest amidite maker), Thermo Fisher (TMO), ChemGenes (private), Merck KGaA (MRK.DE). Captive: Alnylam (Norton MA), Novartis. Shares unverified; top 5 CDMOs likely >60% of outsourced commercial API.
supply_tightness: Moderate. Commercial-scale trains (Cytiva OligoProcess-class synthesizers, large chromatography) take 2-3 years to build and qualify. GMP amidite supply is concentrated (Hongene plus 2-3 Western suppliers), which is a geopolitical chokepoint under BIOSECURE. Acetonitrile and solvent intensity limits single-site scale. Capacity was tight in 2023-25; new trains (Agilent, ST Pharm, Bachem, Nitto) arrive 2025-27. If the CV outcome trials succeed, demand of 3-8 t by 2030 would need several times today's installed capacity, which would tighten supply again in 2028-30.
substitution_risk: Medium-high for the LDL-C/Lp(a) slices. Oral PCSK9 inhibitors (Merck enlicitide, filed 2025, approval timing unverified) and oral Lp(a) inhibitors (Lilly muvalaplin) compete with injectables. One-shot gene editing (Lilly/Verve) is a post-2030 threat. Within manufacturing, enzymatic/ligation processes shift vendor mix (and the value of amidites) without removing demand.
cyclicality_risk: Binary readout risk: a negative HORIZON or OCEAN(a) result would cut the 2030 tonnage case by half or more and strand capacity being built for it. Chinese amidite and CDMO price competition. No double ordering yet.
faster_sub_niche: GalNAc-siRNA/ASO API for cardiovascular indications (and the matching 2'-modified amidites/GalNAc) is the faster slice: ~$0.15-0.9B to $0.6-3.0B (35-50% CAGR), conditional on outcome trials. Rare-disease and neuro oligo API grows ~10-15%. I kept the broader niche because CDMO revenue is not split by indication.

name: Photon-counting CT (PCCT) detector modules - CdTe/CZT crystal + counting ASIC (and deep-silicon)
definition: IN: direct-conversion photon-counting X-ray detector modules for clinical CT, valued at module or transfer price: CdTe/CZT sensor crystals bump-bonded to counting ASICs, or edge-on deep-silicon sensors. OUT: energy-integrating scintillator (GOS) detectors, dual-layer spectral detectors, the rest of the CT gantry and software; industrial/security photon-counting detectors (adjacent, noted only).
value_chain_path: Healthcare -> medical imaging -> computed tomography -> CT detector subsystem -> photon-counting detector modules (CdTe/CZT crystal growth + counting ASIC)
also_serves_megatrends: Aging / cardiology (coronary CT angiography replacing invasive diagnostic angiography)
Compound-semiconductor materials (CdTe also in thin-film solar and security/industrial X-ray inspection of batteries and chips)
size_2026_usd: $0.2-0.6B (own estimate; mostly captive Siemens Healthineers value)
volume_vs_price: Units grow ~3-5x (more OEMs plus lower-tier models). Detector cost per system falls ~30-50% as crystal yields improve and mid-range systems launch, so revenue CAGR is below unit CAGR. Detector $ per CT system is still ~3-5x an energy-integrating detector, which is a content-per-unit tailwind against the installed CT base.
math: 2026: PCCT shipments ~350-600 (almost all Siemens NAEOTOM family) x system price $2.0-3.0M x detector share 25-35% = $0.18-0.63B. 2030: 1,500-3,000 PCCT units (Siemens, GE HealthCare, Canon, Philips, United Imaging; ~8-15% of a global CT market of roughly 15-20k units/yr, unverified) x detector content $0.4-0.7M = $0.6-2.1B. All own estimates; installed-base and unit figures unverified.
catalyst_timing: Siemens NAEOTOM Alpha FDA 510(k) Sep-2021, with lower-cost family members (Alpha.Pro/Peak/Prime) since 2024. GE HealthCare deep-silicon PCCT commercial launch ~2026-27 (FDA timing unverified). Canon CZT PCCT (Redlen) commercial launch ~2026-28 (unverified). Philips and United Imaging entries 2026-28 (unverified). Chest-pain guidelines favoring CCTA-first support cardiac demand.
key_suppliers: Siemens Healthineers (SHL.DE): captive CdTe crystals via Acrorad (Okinawa, JP) and detector production in Germany; est. 85-95% of 2026 PCCT detector value. Canon Medical / Canon Inc. (7751.T): via Redlen Technologies (CZT, Canada; acquired ~2021-22, unverified). GE HealthCare (GEHC, Nasdaq): deep silicon (Prismatic Sensors, SE, acquired 2020). Philips (PHIA.AS). United Imaging (688271.SS). Merchant/material: Kromek (KMK.L; CZT), Varex Imaging (VREX; Direct Conversion, SE), JX Advanced Metals (5016.T; CdTe/CZT substrates), 5N Plus (VNP.TO; high-purity Te/Cd, CZT), Hamamatsu (6965.T).
supply_tightness: High for CdTe/CZT. Growing detector-grade crystals (traveling-heater / vertical Bridgman) has low yields and needs years of process know-how; only ~3-5 producers worldwide can make medical-grade, high-flux crystals, and each OEM is essentially captive to one (Siemens-Acrorad, Canon-Redlen). New OEM qualification takes 2-4 years. Deep silicon (GE) avoids the crystal bottleneck by using silicon foundries.
substitution_risk: Medium-high. Dual-layer spectral CT (Philips) and AI-denoised energy-integrating CT deliver part of the benefit at lower cost. Deep silicon competes with CdTe within the niche (it moves value, not the niche). Hospitals may delay upgrades because CT replacement cycles run 7-10 years.
cyclicality_risk: Medium. Hospital capex cycles, China imaging demand (anti-corruption and VBP slowdown 2023-25), tariffs on imaging equipment, and FX. No double ordering; overbuild risk is low because crystal capacity is scarce.
faster_sub_niche: Merchant CZT/CdTe crystals for non-Siemens OEMs and for industrial PCDs (Kromek, JX, 5N Plus) grow faster from near zero (emerging, <$50M in medical CT in 2026). Deep-silicon modules could grow fastest after 2027 if GE executes. I kept the overall PCCT detector niche because sub-segment data is unavailable.

name: Pulsed-field ablation (PFA) catheters & generators for atrial fibrillation
definition: IN: PFA catheters (single-shot pentaspline/balloon/circular and focal/large-tip, including mapping-integrated designs) and their dedicated generators/consumables for AF ablation. OUT: RF and cryo catheters, standalone 3D mapping capital, ICE catheters, LAAO implants, ventricular ablation tools.
value_chain_path: Healthcare -> cardiovascular devices -> electrophysiology -> AF catheter ablation -> ablation energy modality -> PFA catheters + generators
also_serves_megatrends: Site-of-care shift to ambulatory surgery centers
size_2026_usd: $6-9B (own estimate; supplier sum)
volume_vs_price: ~80-90% volume. AF ablation procedures +12-18%/yr (earlier ablation, persistent AF labels, ASC capacity) and PFA share rising from ~60-70% (2026) to ~85-95% (2030). Blended ASP flat to -3%/yr from four-player competition and China VBP, partly offset by higher-priced mapping-integrated catheters. Not shortage pricing.
math: 2026 top-down: global AF ablations ~1.5-1.9M x PFA share 60-70% = 0.9-1.3M PFA procedures x PFA catheter+consumable revenue $5-7.5k = $4.5-9.8B. Supplier sum (own estimates, unverified): Boston Scientific EP (mostly FARAPULSE) ~$4.0-4.8B + Medtronic PFA (PulseSelect, Affera Sphere-9/360) ~$1.5-2.2B + J&J PFA (Varipulse, dual-energy) ~$0.5-1.0B + Abbott (Volt, TactiFlex Duo) ~$0.2-0.5B + China domestic ~$0.1-0.3B = $6.3-8.8B. 2030: 2.5-3.2M procedures x 88-95% x $4.8-6.5k = $10.6-19.8B.
catalyst_timing: FARAPULSE FDA Jan-2024; persistent AF label 2025. Medtronic Affera Sphere-9 FDA Oct-2024; Sphere-360 approval ~2026-27 (unverified). J&J Varipulse US pause Jan-2025, then dual-energy catheter. Abbott Volt CE Mar-2025, US approval ~late 2025 (unverified). Concomitant PFA+LAAO (OPTION). Possible CMS addition of cardiac ablation to the ASC covered list (unverified).
key_suppliers: Boston Scientific (BSX, NYSE): est. 55-65% PFA share. Medtronic (MDT): ~18-25%. Johnson & Johnson MedTech (JNJ): ~8-12%. Abbott (ABT): ~3-6%. China: MicroPort EP (688351.SS), Sichuan Jinjiang Electronic, APT Medical (688617.SS), Dinova (private), together ~2-4%. Others: Kardium (private, Globe), Field Medical (private), Pulse Biosciences (PLSE). Shares are own estimates.
supply_tightness: Loosened. BSX was capacity-constrained in 2024, but supply is now adequate. Barriers come from the PMA/IDE (3-5 years) plus generator and mapping ecosystem lock-in, not physical capacity. Pricing power is eroding as four multinationals compete.

cyclicality_risk: Low. Constraints are EP lab and staff capacity. China VBP price cuts. No overbuild or double-ordering dynamics.
faster_sub_niche: Mapping-integrated focal/large-footprint PFA catheters (Affera Sphere-9/Sphere-360, BSX Farapoint with Opal mapping, Abbott TactiFlex Duo) likely grow ~25-35% as single-shot share saturates. China PFA conversion (penetration well below the US) has 40%+ volume CAGR but VBP-capped pricing. Neither is separately disclosed.

name: Recombinant hyaluronidase SC-conversion enzymes (ENHANZE rHuPH20, ALT-B4) - royalty/API niche
definition: IN: royalties, milestones and enzyme/API supply revenue from recombinant human hyaluronidase licensed to biopharma for subcutaneous co-formulation of biologics (Halozyme ENHANZE; Alteogen ALT-B4/berahyaluronidase alfa). OUT: underlying drug sales, Halozyme's autoinjector device business and high-concentration formulation tech (Elektrofi) unless enzyme-linked, generic hyaluronidase for ophthalmology/aesthetics.
value_chain_path: Healthcare -> biologic drugs -> drug delivery & formulation -> IV-to-SC conversion -> SC dispersion enzyme (recombinant hyaluronidase) licensing/supply
also_serves_megatrends: Healthcare cost and site-of-care shift (infusion-chair capacity, home/community administration)
Biologic lifecycle management ahead of LOE and IRA price negotiation
size_2026_usd: $1.3-1.8B (own estimate from company disclosures; Halozyme ~80%)
cagr_2026_2030: 8-18% for the whole niche; 35-60% for the Alteogen ALT-B4 sub-niche
volume_vs_price: Royalty rates are contractual, so growth is volume: more SC-converted products and a higher SC share per product. Underlying drug net-price erosion (IRA negotiation, biosimilars) and contractual royalty step-downs (Darzalex late decade, unverified timing) partly offset it. No shortage pricing.
math: 2026: Halozyme royalties ~$1.0-1.25B (Darzalex Faspro, Phesgo, Vyvgart Hytrulo, Opdivo Qvantig, Ocrevus Zunovo, Tecentriq Hybreza, Rybrevant SC) + enzyme/API/milestones ~$0.15-0.25B. Alteogen ~$0.12-0.3B (Keytruda Qlex royalty at a reported low-single-digit rate, unverified, on ~$2-4B Qlex sales, plus milestones and ALT-B4 supply). Total $1.27-1.8B. 2030: Halozyme $1.3-1.9B (Darzalex step-downs offset by Opdivo/Ocrevus/Vyvgart) + Alteogen $0.4-0.9B (Qlex $8-15B x ~2-4%, plus Enhertu SC, AstraZeneca and others) = $1.7-2.8B.
catalyst_timing: Opdivo Qvantig FDA Dec-2024. Keytruda Qlex FDA Sep-2025; EU 2025-26. Merck converting a large share of US Keytruda patients to SC ahead of IV pembrolizumab LOE (~2028). Enhertu SC (Daiichi Sankyo, ALT-B4) Phase 3 ~2026-27. Halozyme vs Merck MDASE patent suit (filed 2025) and PTAB post-grant review decisions ~2026 (unverified).
key_suppliers: Halozyme Therapeutics (HALO, Nasdaq, US): ~75-85% of 2026 niche revenue. Alteogen (196170.KQ, Korea): ~10-20%, rising. Chinese recombinant hyaluronidase developers: unverified, <5%. Shares are own estimates.
supply_tightness: IP-gated duopoly. The enzyme is made at gram scale, so capacity is not a bottleneck. Lock-in is near-total: once a co-formulated product is approved, switching enzymes means a new BLA, so the royalty stream lasts the life of the product.
substitution_risk: Medium. High-concentration enzyme-free SC formulations (Halozyme bought Elektrofi, a hedge), large-volume on-body injectors, and biosimilars of the SC drugs after patent expiry. Patent litigation could redistribute royalties between the two suppliers rather than change total niche size.
cyclicality_risk: Low economic cyclicality. Litigation, IRA negotiation of Darzalex/Keytruda (lower net prices mean lower royalty $) and lumpy milestones (Alteogen) are the risks.
faster_sub_niche: Alteogen ALT-B4 (Keytruda Qlex, Enhertu SC, AstraZeneca and others): ~$0.12-0.3B to $0.4-0.9B, a 35-60% CAGR, but milestone-lumpy. Halozyme alone is ~5-12% after 2027 as Darzalex matures. The whole niche is probably too slow to rank economy-wide; the Alteogen slice is the candidate.

name: Quartz (Q-glass) fiber cloth for M9-class ultra-low-loss CCL
definition: IN: woven fabric of fused-silica fiber (SiO2 >=99.9%), and the quartz yarn sold to make it, in thin electronic styles used to reinforce M9-and-above CCL and prepreg. Approximate properties: Dk ~3.7-3.8, Df ~0.0001-0.0002. Uses: AI-server midplanes, orthogonal backplanes, 224G/448G-SerDes switch boards and high-end ASIC boards. OUT: E-glass, Low-Dk1 (NE-class) and Low-Dk2 glass cloth; quartz fiber for radomes and aerospace; quartz tubes and crucibles; PTFE laminates.
value_chain_path: AI data centers -> AI server/switch racks -> high-layer PCBs (midplane, orthogonal backplane, switch tray) -> M9-class ultra-low-loss CCL/prepreg -> glass-fiber reinforcement -> quartz (Q-glass) fiber cloth (and quartz yarn)
also_serves_megatrends: Defense radomes (adjacent quartz-fiber demand that competes for yarn)
size_2026_usd: US$60-250M (own estimate; low confidence; unverified in-session)
volume_vs_price: Almost entirely volume. Cloth area could grow 70-120% a year from a small base while price per m2 falls an estimated 30-50% from 2026 to 2030 as Chinese capacity scales. 2026 pricing reflects scarcity during qualification and should not be extrapolated.
math: Top-down 2026: M9 board area of 0.05-0.15M m2 (first Rubin-generation midplane and CPX-type boards plus early switch boards; own estimate) x ~40 cloth plies per m2 of finished 30-40-layer board / 0.7 panel utilization = ~3-9M m2 of cloth. At US$15-35/m2 (unverified; Q-cloth is reported at several times Low-Dk1 and tens of times E-glass per meter) that gives ~US$45-300M. Top-down 2030: M9+ board area of 0.8-2.0M m2 (Kyber-type orthogonal backplanes, next-generation compute boards, 448G switches) x 40 / 0.75 = ~43-107M m2. At US$10-20/m2 that gives ~US$0.45-2.1B. Bottom-up: no supplier separately discloses Q-cloth revenue that I can confirm; Feilihua's quartz electronic-cloth line is the best single disclosure to check (unverified).
catalyst_timing: 2H26: Rubin-generation rack ramp (Nvidia said at CES in Jan 2026 that Vera Rubin was in full production). 2H27: Rubin Ultra Kyber racks with PCB orthogonal backplanes. 2028: Feynman generation. 2028-29: 448G-SerDes switch silicon. Qualification windows at CCL makers (EMC, TUC, Doosan, Panasonic) run 2026-27.
key_suppliers: Feilihua (300395.SZ, China): integrated from quartz sand to fiber to cloth, likely the largest 2026 cloth shipper (share unverified, guess 30-50%). Shin-Etsu Chemical / Shin-Etsu Quartz Products (4063.T, Japan): quartz yarn and cloth. Saint-Gobain Quartz (SGO.PA, France): Quartzel yarn. Sinoma Science & Technology (002080.SZ, China). Grace Fabric Technology (603256.SH, China). Nittobo (3110.T) and Asahi Kasei (3407.T) in development or qualification. Taiwan Glass (1802.TW) reportedly developing. All shares unverified.
supply_tightness: The bottleneck is yarn. Quartz fiber is drawn from high-purity fused-silica rods at ~2,000C; few qualified yarn makers exist and the fiber is brittle, so loom speeds and weaving yields are well below E-glass. CCL qualification at Nvidia-tier OEMs takes ~6-12 months. Capacity is being added mainly in China (2025-27). Pricing power is very high now, but this is scarcity pricing during qualification (unverified).
substitution_risk: High. Low-Dk2 / next-generation low-Dk glass plus HVLP4 may be good enough, and hybrid stack-ups may use Q-cloth only in critical signal layers. Quartz wears drills 5-10x faster, which raises board cost and motivates substitution. Architecture shifts (copper cable vs PCB midplane, earlier CPO) could cut M9 board area. PTFE and hydrocarbon laminates are alternatives.
cyclicality_risk: High. Concentrated on one customer roadmap (Nvidia). CCL makers may double-order during 2026-27 qualification. Several Chinese entrants (Feilihua, Sinoma, Grace and others) adding capacity at once creates a real 2028+ overbuild risk with sharp ASP compression.
faster_sub_niche: Split: Low-Dk glass cloth overall (Low-Dk1 + Low-Dk2) is about US$0.8-1.5B in 2026 at ~20-30% CAGR (own estimate, unverified). Q-glass is the faster sub-segment at 45-90%. Within Q-glass, quartz yarn is the tighter bottleneck and has more pricing power than weaving.

name: HVLP4/HVLP5 hyper-very-low-profile copper foil for M8/M9 high-speed CCL
definition: IN: electrodeposited copper foil, mainly 12-35 um, whose bonding-side roughness is at the HVLP4/HVLP5 grades (Rz roughly 0.5 um or below; vendor-specific; unverified spec bounds). It is sold to CCL makers for M8/M9 laminates used in 112G/224G-SerDes AI-server, switch and optical-module boards. OUT: HVLP1-3, RTF/VLP, standard HTE foil, lithium-battery foil, ultra-thin carrier foil for substrates, rolled-annealed foil.
value_chain_path: AI data centers -> AI server/switch racks -> high-layer PCBs -> M8/M9 low-loss CCL -> electrodeposited copper foil -> HVLP4/HVLP5 grade
size_2026_usd: US$150-400M for HVLP4/5 only (own estimate; low confidence). All HVLP grades 1-5: ~US$0.6-1.2B (own estimate).
volume_vs_price: ~70-80% volume, from growth in M8/M9 board area and the mix shift from HVLP2/3 to HVLP4/5. ~20-30% price, from elevated processing fees while qualified capacity is scarce. Copper pass-through adds noise: record copper prices in 2026 inflate revenue without adding margin. Expect processing-fee compression from 2028 as Chinese HVLP4 qualifies.
math: Per m2 of a 24-40-layer M8/M9 board: ~50-60% of copper layers are signal layers using HVLP4/5. That is 12-24 m2 of foil / 0.75 utilization = 16-32 m2, x 0.11-0.16 kg/m2 (12-18 um) = ~2-5 kg of HVLP4/5 per m2 of board. 2026: 0.6-1.2M m2 of M8/M9 boards = 1.2-6k t, plus switch, optical-module and ASIC boards, for ~3-9k t in total. At US$30-45k/t (copper ~US$10-12k/t plus an unverified HVLP4 premium of ~US$20-30k/t) that is ~US$90-400M. 2030: 3-6M m2 x 3-5 kg = 9-30k t plus other boards, ~15-35k t at US$28-40k/t = ~US$0.4-1.4B. Bottom-up: Mitsui, Furukawa, Fukuda, Circuit Foil, Chang Chun, Co-Tech and Nan Ya do not split out HVLP4/5 revenue (unverified).
catalyst_timing: 2025-26: M8 adoption on GB300-class boards and 1.6T switches. 2H26: Rubin (M8/M9). 2027: Kyber backplanes. 2028+: 448G SerDes, which needs HVLP5 or a successor ultra-smooth process. CCL and OEM qualification windows run 2026-27.
key_suppliers: Mitsui Mining & Smelting (5706.T, Japan); Furukawa Electric (5801.T, Japan); Fukuda Metal Foil & Powder (5821.T, Japan); Circuit Foil Luxembourg (Solus Advanced Materials, 336370.KS, Korea-owned); Chang Chun Group (private, Taiwan); Co-Tech Development (8358.TWO, Taiwan); Nan Ya Plastics (1303.TW). Chinese challengers: Defu Technology (301511.SZ), Tongguan Copper Foil (301217.SZ) and others in qualification. Japanese makers plus CFL probably hold more than half of 2026 HVLP4 (own estimate, unverified).
supply_tightness: HVLP4/5 needs proprietary low-profile nodule treatment and adhesion chemistry, tight thickness and pinhole control, and 9-18 months of qualification across CCL maker and OEM. New foil lines take ~18-24 months. Converting battery-foil lines is possible, but holding quality is hard. Taiwan media reported tightness and higher processing fees in 2025-26 (unverified magnitude).
substitution_risk: Medium. Alternatives include smoother foil from new processes (sputtered or PVD-assisted copper), adhesion promoters that let HVLP3 perform like HVLP4, and long-term reach reduction from CPO and shorter electrical paths. The bigger risk is pricing (Chinese processing-fee competition) rather than outright substitution.
cyclicality_risk: Copper price volatility; a Chinese electrodeposited-foil glut (battery-foil overcapacity) migrating into HVLP; double ordering around the Rubin ramp; customer concentration in Nvidia-chain CCL.
faster_sub_niche: Split: HVLP1-3 grows ~10-20% with eroding ASP; HVLP4/5 grows 35-55% (chosen). HVLP5 alone is faster still, but it is below ~US$50M in 2026 (emerging) and tied to 448G timing in 2028+.

name: Low-CTE (T-glass-class) glass cloth for IC-substrate cores and prepregs
definition: IN: woven cloth, and its yarn, made from low-thermal-expansion high-modulus glass: CTE ~2.5-3 ppm/K versus ~5.5 for E-glass (Nittobo 'T-glass' and equivalents). It comes in thin styles (<=100 um) for BT and ABF substrate core laminates and prepregs, and is sold to laminate makers such as MGC, Resonac, Doosan and Nan Ya. OUT: low-Dk cloth for server CCL, E-glass cloth, solid glass-core panels, ABF film itself.
value_chain_path: AI/HPC chips + memory -> advanced packages -> IC substrates (ABF FC-BGA, BT) -> core laminate / prepreg -> glass reinforcement -> low-CTE (T-glass) cloth
also_serves_megatrends: Smartphone and PC application processors (Apple, Qualcomm, MediaTek)
size_2026_usd: US$250-600M (own estimate; low-medium confidence; unverified)
volume_vs_price: 2026-27 is price-led, with allocation pricing and increases of roughly 10-25% (unverified). 2028-30 is volume-led as Nittobo's capacity additions and second sources arrive. Overall ~70% volume and ~30% price. Price could retrace in 2029-30 once Taiwan and Chinese entrants are qualified.
math: Top-down: IC substrate market 2026 ~US$15-18B (Prismark-type range; unverified). Glass cloth is ~2-4% of substrate value at T-glass pricing, giving ~US$300-700M. Content driver: AI package body size has grown from ~55 mm (2022) to 75-100 mm (2025-27) and is heading to 120 mm+ (2028+), so area per package rises 2-4x and layer counts reach 16-24. Low-CTE cloth per AI package therefore rises several-fold per generation. Capacity-bound 2030: Nittobo's reported multi-fold expansion (~2-3x by 2027-28; unverified) plus entrants adding ~30-50% gives ~2.5-3.5x volume. With ASP flat to -10%, revenue grows ~2.2-3.0x, about 22-32% CAGR. Demand-bound check: high-end substrate area growing ~15-20% a year plus BT memory recovery points to ~18-25%.
catalyst_timing: Shortage reported since mid/late 2025. Nittobo's new capacity is reported to arrive 2H26 to 2027-28. Rubin, TPU and Trainium-class large-body substrates ramp 2026-27, alongside the memory-package upcycle. Glass-core substitution starts at the margin in 2028-30.
key_suppliers: Nitto Boseki (3110.T, Japan): dominant, est. ~70-90% of T-glass-class supply in 2025 (third-party commentary; unverified). Challengers: Grace Fabric Technology (603256.SH, China), Taiwan Glass (1802.TW), Fulltech Fiber Glass (1815.TW), Sinoma/Taishan (002080.SZ), AGY (private, US; S-type glass yarn). Laminate chokepoint downstream: Mitsubishi Gas Chemical (4182.T) for BT.
supply_tightness: Severe in 2025-26. Apple, Nvidia, Qualcomm and AMD reportedly competed for allocation while substrate makers (Ibiden, Unimicron, Kinsus, Nan Ya PCB, SEMCO) qualified second sources. Low-CTE glass needs dedicated high-temperature furnaces and Pt-Rh bushings, with lead times of 2+ years. Substrate-core qualification takes 12-24 months because of warpage and reliability, so pricing power is high through ~2027.
substitution_risk: Medium. Glass-core substrates (2028-30) remove cloth from cores for some AI packages. Low-CTE resin systems with NE/E-glass, coreless designs, and Chinese/Taiwan second sources mainly threaten price rather than volume.
cyclicality_risk: High after 2027. Panic and double ordering in 2025-26, Nittobo's multi-fold build-out and new entrants together create a 2028-29 oversupply risk. Smartphone and memory cycles add volatility.
faster_sub_niche: Cloth for ABF cores in large AI packages (>=75 mm) likely grows 30-40%, versus ~10-15% for BT/mobile low-CTE cloth. The split is soft because both share furnaces and yarn, so I analyse the combined niche and flag the AI share as the growth engine.

name: AI-grade coated carbide micro-drills (high-aspect-ratio and backdrill) for high-layer AI-server PCBs
definition: IN: tungsten-carbide PCB drill bits, about 0.1-0.35 mm for vias up to ~3 mm, high-aspect-ratio (>=20:1), coated (ta-C / DLC / diamond). Includes backdrill bits and regrinding services, used on 20-70+ layer, 3-8 mm-thick boards built on M7-M9 laminates (low-Dk2 and quartz cloth). OUT: standard FR-4/HDI drills for consumer boards, router bits, CNC and laser drilling equipment.
value_chain_path: AI data centers -> AI server/switch boards -> PCB fabrication -> mechanical drilling and backdrilling -> AI-grade coated carbide micro-drills (consumable)
size_2026_usd: US$250-500M AI-grade (own estimate; low confidence), within a total PCB micro-drill market of ~US$1.0-1.6B (own estimate; unverified)
volume_vs_price: ~60-70% volume: bits consumed per m2 of board rise 3-10x versus FR-4 because low-Dk2 and quartz cloth are abrasive and backdrilling adds passes. ~30-40% price and mix: long coated bits sell at 2-5x commodity ASP. Pass-through of record tungsten (APT) prices in 2025-26 is the non-durable part of price growth.
math: 2026: AI/high-speed board area of 2-4M m2 (own estimate) x 150-300k holes per m2 including backdrill passes, divided by effective hits per bit including regrinds (~1,000-2,500 on M7/M8, ~300-800 on M9/quartz), gives ~150-500 bits per m2. That is ~0.3-1.6B bits at US$0.3-0.8 each, or ~US$0.1-1.0B (central ~US$350M). Cross-check against supplier revenue (all unverified): Dingtai total sales roughly US$250-350M, with an AI-grade share still to be confirmed; Union Tool PCB drills ~US$150-250M; Topoint ~US$80-150M. Summing their AI-grade portions gives roughly US$250-450M. 2030: 5-9M m2 of boards x 200-700 bits/m2 (more M9) x US$0.35-0.8 is a very wide range with a central ~US$1.0-1.2B. Better coatings that extend bit life are the main downside lever.
catalyst_timing: 2H26 Rubin ramp; 2027 Kyber orthogonal backplanes (very thick boards); 2027-28 adoption of quartz-cloth M9, where drill life collapses; 2026-27 capacity additions at Dingtai and Union Tool.
key_suppliers: Shenzhen Dingtai High-Tech (301377.SZ, China): global #1 by volume, est. ~25-30% share (unverified). Union Tool (6278.T, Japan): strong in high-end. Topoint Technology (8021.TW, Taiwan). Jinzhou Precision (subsidiary of China Tungsten High-Tech, 000657.SZ). KYOCERA Precision Tools (6971.T). Shares unverified.
supply_tightness: Inputs are sub-micron WC-Co rod, precision grinding machines with long lead times, and coating capacity. Taiwan and Chinese media reported supply shortfalls ('供不應求') for AI-grade bits in 2025-26 (unverified). Tungsten raw-material cost is up sharply under Chinese export controls (unverified level). PCB makers qualify bits per laminate type, so switching takes weeks to months; this is less of a barrier than for materials.
substitution_risk: Low-medium. Laser drilling serves microvias, not thick through-holes. The real offset is longer bit life (diamond / ta-C coatings, better regrinding), which cuts unit demand. Cable, CPO or architecture changes could also shrink AI board area.
cyclicality_risk: Medium. PCB capacity cycle; tungsten price reversal deflates revenue; aggressive capacity additions by Chinese leaders; channel stocking during 2026 shortage headlines.
faster_sub_niche: Split: commodity FR-4/HDI drills grow ~3-6% versus AI-grade at 25-40% (chosen). Within AI-grade, quartz-capable diamond-coated drills grow fastest but are a 2027+ story tied to Q-glass adoption.

evidence.label: reported fact

evidence.claim: Dingtai filings should disclose drill output and capacity in pieces per month, price trend, and AI-server share; Chinese media reported it as supply-constrained. Unverified in-session.
evidence.label: reported fact
evidence.source: Shenzhen Dingtai High-Tech (301377.SZ) filings on CNINFO; Cailian Press

evidence.label: reported fact

evidence.label: own estimate

name: Advanced MEMS probe cards for HBM and leading-edge AI logic wafer sort
definition: IN: advanced MEMS probe cards, plus replacement probe heads and probes, for wafer sort of (a) HBM DRAM core and base dies and known-good-stack test, and (b) N3/N2/A16 AI accelerator, ASIC, CPU and chiplet dies destined for CoWoS-class packages. OUT: cards for mature logic, NAND and commodity DRAM; probers and ATE testers; final-test sockets.
value_chain_path: AI data centers -> AI accelerators + HBM -> wafer-level test (sort) -> probe interface -> advanced MEMS probe cards for HBM / AI logic
also_serves_megatrends: Chiplet / known-good-die test for all advanced packaging
size_2026_usd: US$0.9-1.4B (own estimate), within a total probe-card market of ~US$3.0-3.8B (third-party-type range; unverified)
volume_vs_price: ~55% volume: HBM bit and stack growth, more chiplets per package, rising known-good-die test coverage and more touchdowns. ~45% ASP and mix: HBM4/4E pin counts with finer pitch, high-current probes for 1-3 kW dies, at-temperature test. This is mostly design-driven, not shortage pricing.
math: Bottom-up 2026 (supplier revenue, all unverified): FormFactor HBM/AI-related ~US$300-400M; MJC HBM ~US$250-350M; Technoprobe AI/HPC logic ~US$250-350M; MPI and CHPT AI-related ~US$150-250M; others ~US$50M. Total ~US$1.0-1.4B. 2030: the HBM probe-card pool grows with HBM revenue (25-35% a year), and the AI-logic pool grows with leading-edge AI wafer starts plus chiplet count (15-25% a year). Blended ~18-28%, giving ~US$2.0-3.2B.
catalyst_timing: 2026: HBM4 ramp for Rubin. 2027: HBM4E and custom HBM base dies on logic processes, where each customer needs new card designs. 2026-27: N2 AI chips. 2027-28: A16.
key_suppliers: FormFactor (FORM, US; overall #1, est. ~25-30%); Technoprobe (TPRO.MI, Italy; ~20-25%); MJC Micronics Japan (6871.T; strong at SK hynix and Micron HBM); Japan Electronic Materials (6855.T); MPI (6223.TW); Chunghwa Precision Test Tech (CHPT, 6510.TW); TSE (131290.KQ, Korea). faster_sub_niche: HBM probe cards, including base-die and stack test, likely grow 25-35% versus 15-25% for AI-logic cards. HBM is faster but more cyclical; I keep both because the supplier sets overlap and the split is not disclosed.

name: AI-server-grade high-capacitance / high-voltage MLCCs
definition: IN: MLCCs specified for AI servers and racks: high capacitance (about 10-100 uF in 0402-1210 sizes), high temperature (X6S/X7R/X7T), low-ESL types around accelerator power delivery, and 100-630 V parts for 48 V and emerging 800 V DC rails and power shelves. OUT: general consumer and handset MLCCs, automotive-only lines, silicon/deep-trench capacitors, tantalum and aluminum polymer capacitors.
value_chain_path: AI data centers -> AI racks (compute trays, power shelves, switch trays) -> board power-delivery network -> passive components -> AI-server-grade MLCC
also_serves_megatrends: EV / ADAS (shares high-cap and high-voltage lines)
size_2026_usd: US$1.5-2.8B (own estimate; low confidence), within a total MLCC market of ~US$13-16B (unverified)
volume_vs_price: ~70% volume and ~30% mix/ASP. AI grades are stable to slightly up while commodity MLCC prices stay soft. 2026 surcharges from silver and other metals are cost-push, not durable.
math: 2026: 12-16M accelerators x US$80-150 of MLCC content per accelerator, including its share of tray, NIC and power-shelf content (own estimate; a GB200-class rack carrying a few hundred thousand MLCCs is consistent with this) = ~US$1.0-2.4B. Adding AI-server CPUs, switches and power gives ~US$1.5-2.8B. 2030: 25-40M accelerator-equivalents x US$100-160 = ~US$2.5-6.4B. Content rises with TDP: ~1.2 kW (B200) to ~1.8-2.3 kW (Rubin) to ~3+ kW (Rubin Ultra, unverified).
catalyst_timing: 2H26 Rubin; 2027 Rubin Ultra; 2027-28 800 V DC rack architectures, which add high-voltage MLCC demand; Murata and SEMCO capacity additions 2026-28.
key_suppliers: Murata (6981.T; est. ~40%+ of high-end); Samsung Electro-Mechanics (009150.KS; ~20-25%); Taiyo Yuden (6976.T); TDK (6762.T); Kyocera AVX (6971.T); Yageo (2327.TW). Mid-range Chinese suppliers: Fenghua Advanced (000636.SZ), CCTC Three-Circle (300408.SZ). Shares unverified.
supply_tightness: Moderate. Thin-layer (<=~0.5 um) high-cap know-how and nano barium-titanate powder (Japanese suppliers) are the barriers. Lead times on some AI grades were reported extended in 2026 (unverified), but Murata and SEMCO have large capacity, so there is no hard bottleneck.
substitution_risk: Medium. Silicon/deep-trench and embedded capacitors in interposers and substrates take package-level decoupling. Vertical power delivery modules relocate content to the module makers' bill of materials, mostly still MLCC. Polymer capacitors serve bulk needs.
cyclicality_risk: High historically (2018 shortage, then crash). Channel inventory swings; Chinese capacity in mid-range grades.
faster_sub_niche: High-voltage (>=250 V) MLCC for 800 V DC power shelves and racks could grow 40%+ after 2027 from a sub-US$200M base (unverified). It is too early to size reliably, so I keep the broader AI grade.

name: LEAP-1A/-1B engine shop-visit MRO (labor + OEM material)
definition: IN: revenue from off-wing shop visits on CFM LEAP-1A (A320neo family), LEAP-1B (737 MAX) and LEAP-1C (C919). That covers performance restorations, hot-section and LLP-driven workscopes, OEM spare parts and LLPs used in those visits, and labor at both OEM shops (GE, Safran) and CFM-licensed independents. OUT: CFM56, PW1100G GTF, V2500, widebody engines, line/on-wing maintenance, spare-engine leasing and new-engine OE sales.
value_chain_path: Commercial aerospace -> aero engines -> engine aftermarket services -> new-generation narrowbody engine MRO -> LEAP-1A/1B shop visits -> (faster sub) LLP stacks & HPT hot-section replacement parts
size_2026_usd: US$5-8B (own estimate; fleet/shop-visit model, not re-verified)
volume_vs_price: About 70% volume, 30% price/workscope. Shop visits rise roughly 18-25%/yr as the 2016-2025 delivery cohorts reach first and second removals. Revenue per visit rises about 6-9%/yr: CFM catalog price escalation of roughly 4-6%/yr, plus deeper LLP-driven workscopes from ~2027. The volume part is durable because it is driven by fleet age. The catalog-price part partly reflects scarcity pricing and could slow if spare-parts supply catches up.
math: Fleet: LEAP deliveries 2016-2024 = 77+459+1,118+1,736+815+845+1,136+1,570+1,407 = 9,163 engines (reported annual figures). 2025 is about 1,650-1,800 (guidance was +15-20%), so about 10.8-11.0k engines by YE2025. Adding about 2.0-2.4k/yr in 2026-2030 (A320neo rate-75 and 737 rate 47-52 plans, LEAP about 60% of A320neo, 100% of MAX, about 10% spares) gives about 21-23k by YE2030. Shop visits by cohort, with annual SV rates: 2016-19 cohort (~3.4k engines) 15% in 2026 rising to 20% in 2030; 2020-22 cohort (~2.8k) 8% to 18%; 2023-25 cohort (~4.7k) 4% to 15%; post-2026 cohort about 3% hot-and-harsh early removals. That gives about 1,000-1,400 SVs in 2026 and about 2,200-3,000 in 2030. Revenue per SV (labor plus material): $4.5-6M in 2026 and $6.5-8.5M in 2030. So 2026 is about $5-8B and 2030 about $14-22B. Bottom-up cross-check: GE Commercial Engines & Services revenue was about $27B in 2024, about 70% services (about $19B, unverified approximation). LEAP is a minority but the fastest-growing slice. CFM aftermarket is shared 50/50 GE/Safran, and independent shops add about $1-2B of labor. Both views are consistent with about $6-8B in 2026 (own estimate).
catalyst_timing: 2026-2028: first-run removals of the 2020-2023 delivery cohorts. 2025-2028: retrofits of the LEAP-1A HPT durability kit. 2027-2031: LLP-driven second shop visits of the 2016-2019 cohort (around 9-12 years at 1,800-2,200 cycles/yr; exact LEAP LLP lives unverified). 2026-2027: CFM56 shop visits plateau and then fall, freeing shop capacity and steering independents to LEAP. New LEAP lines at GE, Safran, StandardAero, MTU, Lufthansa Technik, Delta TechOps and AFI KLM ramp in 2025-2028.
key_suppliers: CFM International (GE Aerospace NYSE:GE 50% / Safran EPA:SAF 50%) supplies about 65-75% of shop-visit value as OEM material; OEM-owned shops do about 50-60% of LEAP SV labor today (own estimate). CFM-licensed and 'Premier MRO' independents: StandardAero (NYSE:SARO), MTU Maintenance (XETRA:MTX), Lufthansa Technik (Lufthansa XETRA:LHA), AFI KLM E&M (EPA:AF), Delta TechOps (NYSE:DAL), ST Engineering (SGX:S63). Independents' combined labor share is about 40-50% and rising (own estimate). Castings and forgings behind the spares: PCC (Berkshire BRK), Howmet (NYSE:HWM).
supply_tightness: Tight. Tech data and parts are controlled through CFM licenses, so pricing power is high. HPT blades and LLP forgings come from the same casting/forging base as OE engines, and the OEMs have repeatedly had to ration between OE and spares. Turn times are long (roughly 90-150+ days, unverified), test-cell and skilled-technician capacity is limited, and LEAP spare-engine lease rates are high (unverified). Adding a new licensed LEAP line takes about 2-3 years (license, tooling, test-cell correlation).
substitution_risk: Low to moderate. PMA and DER repairs are limited on LEAP because CFM restricts them and lessors resist them; this could loosen after 2028. Durability kits lengthen time-on-wing, which lowers SV frequency but raises parts content. GTF competes only on A320neo (about 35-40% share), and its reliability problems push more flying onto LEAP aircraft. No substitute for shop visits exists.
cyclicality_risk: Moderate. A traffic recession would defer shop visits, but young-fleet LEAP visits are less deferrable than CFM56 ones, which can use green-time swaps and USM. Risk of double counting: airline and lessor spare-engine buying in 2024-2026 partly reflects shortage, not structural need. Catalog pricing could reset if parts supply normalizes around 2028.
faster_sub_niche: LEAP LLP stacks plus new-make HPT hot-section spares (OEM material only). About US$1.5-3B in 2026 growing to US$6-11B in 2030, a CAGR of roughly 35-45% (own estimate, low confidence). The driver is second-run shop visits of the 2016-2019 cohort reaching LLP limits from ~2027, plus durability-kit HPT blade retrofits. CFM (GE/Safran) is effectively the only source until LEAP teardown/USM supply builds after ~2030. SPLIT NOTE: PW1100G GTF MRO is excluded and grows more slowly after 2027 (about 8-15%), because 2024-2026 volumes are inflated by the powder-metal disk inspection campaign. CFM56/V2500 MRO is flat to declining after ~2027.

name: Hot-gas-path SX/DS airfoil castings for large-frame industrial gas turbines (OE + spares)
definition: IN: investment-cast nickel-superalloy blades (buckets) and vanes (nozzles), equiaxed, directionally solidified or single-crystal, for turbine stages 1-4 of heavy-duty E/F/H/J-class gas turbines (>~150 MW). Valued at the casting-house level (cast, machined, and coated where the caster coats), for both new units and aftermarket replacement sets. OUT: aero-engine airfoils; OEM resale markup on spares; hot-gas-path repair services; combustion hardware; rotors; HRSGs.
value_chain_path: Heavy industrial / power (aero overlap) -> gas turbines -> large-frame F/H/J-class GT -> hot-gas-path components -> SX/DS investment-cast blades & vanes -> (faster sub) large SX stage-1/2 airfoils for new H/J-class units
also_serves_megatrends: aero-engine ramp (shared SX furnace and ceramic-core capacity)
energy security / coal-to-gas switching (Asia, Middle East)
size_2026_usd: US$3.0-4.5B (own estimate)
cagr_2026_2030: 10-16% (whole niche); faster OE sub-niche 15-20% through 2028, then flattening
volume_vs_price: About 60-65% volume, 35-40% price. New-unit volume grows roughly 9-12%/yr as GE Vernova, Siemens Energy and MHI add capacity. Aftermarket volume grows roughly 5-8%/yr with higher capacity factors. Price adds about 4-6%/yr through long-term agreements with escalators and scarcity premia. The price share is higher than in LEAP MRO, so growth is less durable once casters add furnaces around 2027-2029.
math: Top-down (own estimate). Heavy-duty GT output: GE Vernova about 20 GW/yr run-rate from 2H26 (company target), Siemens Energy about 15-20 GW, MHI about 12-20 GW (plans to roughly double), others (Ansaldo, Doosan, Chinese licensees) about 5-8 GW. Total about 52-68 GW in 2026, rising to 75-95 GW in 2029-30. At about 300-350 MW average that is roughly 160-210 units in 2026 and 230-290 units in 2030. OE castings at about $3-6M per unit (about 200-300 airfoils, ASP $5-60k each; stage-1/2 SX dominate value): about $0.6-1.2B in 2026 and $1.0-1.9B in 2030. Aftermarket: about 2,500-3,000 F/H/J units installed, a hot-gas-path set every about 3-4 years at baseload, about 600-800 sets/yr at about $3-4M casting value, plus E-class. That is about $2.0-3.3B in 2026 growing 7-11%/yr. Total 2026 about $3.0-4.5B. Bottom-up cross-check (all unverified own estimates): Howmet IGT about $0.8-1.1B, PCC Airfoils IGT about $1.0-1.5B, Doncasters about $0.3-0.5B, CPP about $0.2-0.4B, Chromalloy about $0.2-0.4B, Yingliu about $0.1-0.2B, captive (MHI Takasago, Doosan, Chinese OEMs) about $0.5-1.0B. Sum about $3.1-5.1B, consistent.
catalyst_timing: GE Vernova reaches about 20 GW/yr in 2H26 and has signalled about 24 GW/yr around 2028 (unverified). MHI's capacity doubling lands around 2026-2027. Siemens Energy (Berlin/Charlotte) expansions run 2026-2028. Slot reservations stretch into 2029-2030. The US data-center firm-power build peaks 2026-2029. Rising aftermarket demand from higher capacity factors is visible from 2026.
key_suppliers: PCC / PCC Airfoils (Berkshire Hathaway NYSE:BRK), about 30-35%. Howmet Aerospace (NYSE:HWM), about 25-30%. Doncasters (UK, private), about 8-10%. Consolidated Precision Products (US, private), about 5-8%. Chromalloy (US, private), about 5%. Kocel/Yingliu Group (SSE:603308), about 3-5% and rising (exports to Western OEMs). Captive foundries (MHI 7011.T Takasago; Doosan Enerbility KRX:034020; Harbin/Dongfang/Shanghai Electric licensees), about 15-20%. All shares are own estimates. Bottleneck inputs: ceramic cores (Morgan Advanced Materials LSE:MGAM, CoorsTek private, captive) and SX master alloy with rhenium (Cannon-Muskegon/PCC, Molymet).
supply_tightness: Very tight. There are few houses qualified for large SX castings (PCC, Howmet, and in part Doncasters, CPP, Yingliu). New SX/DS furnaces take about 12-24 months to arrive, and each part number takes about 12-36 months to qualify with the OEM. Yield on large SX blades is low, which multiplies core and alloy demand. Aero programs compete for the same furnaces and cores. Casters are signing long-term agreements to 2030+ with escalators, and the OEMs are raising new-unit prices (direction reported; magnitude unverified).
substitution_risk: Low inside the gas turbine, since nothing replaces SX/DS for stage 1-2. CMC shrouds and vanes for IGT could arrive after ~2028 (too early). Additive manufacturing is limited to burners and some vanes. Hot-gas-path repair and life extension (Chromalloy, EthosEnergy, Sulzer) replaces some new-make spares. At system level, reciprocating engines, fuel cells (Bloom), batteries and grid supply compete for marginal data-center power. Doosan and Chinese GTs are a regional threat.
cyclicality_risk: HIGH historically: gas turbines had a boom-bust in 2000-2002 and a slump in 2017-2019. Slot reservations from hyperscalers and IPPs may be duplicated across OEMs (double ordering). If AI capex slows, 2029-2030 OE castings could fall. Overbuilt casting capacity around 2028-2029 would erode the pricing share of growth.
faster_sub_niche: OE large single-crystal stage-1/2 blades and vanes for new H/J-class units, about 15-20% CAGR through 2028 and then flat. H/J-class carries more SX content than F-class. Aeroderivative and small industrial GT castings (LM2500/LM6000, FT8, SGT-800, Solar Titan) are similarly fast (about 15-25% in 2026-2028, own estimate), driven by behind-the-meter data-center power. They are more reversible once grid connections catch up, and they compete directly with aero-engine airfoils for foundry capacity. SPLIT NOTE: aftermarket replacement sets (about 7-11%) slow the blended niche.

name: SiC/SiC ceramic-matrix-composite (CMC) hot-section components for aero engines
definition: IN: SiC-fiber-reinforced SiC-matrix parts (melt-infiltrated or CVI): HPT shrouds, HPT nozzles/vanes, combustor liners and exhaust components, for commercial and military aero engines, both new-build and replacement spares. Includes value captured upstream in SiC fiber and prepreg. OUT: C/SiC brake discs (automotive/aircraft brakes), oxide-oxide CMC for nacelle and exhaust plugs, hypersonic/space thermal protection, and IGT CMC (tracked as too early).
value_chain_path: Commercial aerospace -> aero engines -> hot section -> high-temperature materials -> SiC/SiC CMC components -> (input) SiC fiber
size_2026_usd: US$0.3-0.6B (own estimate)
volume_vs_price: About 85-90% volume and content, about 10-15% price. Growth comes from LEAP OE and spares volume, the GE9X ramp (about $0.4-0.8M CMC content per engine versus about $40-80k on LEAP), and more CMC part numbers per engine generation. Pricing is set under OEM-captive transfer pricing, so it is not shortage-driven.
math: Own estimate. LEAP: CMC HPT shroud content about $40-80k per engine. OE about 2,000-2,200 engines in 2026 gives $80-180M; about 2,400-2,700 in 2030 gives $100-215M. Spares: shrouds replaced at shop visits, about 1,000-1,400 SVs in 2026 rising to 2,200-3,000 in 2030, gives $40-110M in 2026 and $90-240M in 2030. GE9X (5 CMC part types, about $0.4-0.8M per engine): about 50-80 engines in 2026 rising to 150-250/yr in 2029-30, gives $20-60M in 2026 and $60-200M in 2030. Military, Safran, RR and other uses: about $50-150M in 2026 and $150-400M in 2030. Total about $0.3-0.6B in 2026 and $0.7-1.4B in 2030, a CAGR of about 18-28%. Generic 'CMC market' reports (US$10B+, including brakes) are low quality and not used.
catalyst_timing: 777X/GE9X first delivery was pushed to 2027 (Boeing, Oct-2025), and the ramp runs 2027-2030. LEAP OE rate above 2,000/yr and spares at shop visits over 2026-2030. Military adaptive-engine and NGAP programs run late decade. RISE/open-fan (heavy CMC use) and IGT CMC come after 2030 and after 2028 respectively.
key_suppliers: GE Aerospace (NYSE:GE), captive, about 70-80% (Asheville NC parts; Huntsville AL SiC fiber and prepreg). Safran Ceramics (EPA:SAF), about 10%. Rolls-Royce High Temperature Composites (LSE:RR), about 5%. COI Ceramics (Northrop Grumman NYSE:NOC), a few %. Chinese AECC institutes are captive in China. SiC fiber: NGS Advanced Fibers (JV of Nippon Carbon TYO:5302, GE and Safran) and Ube (TYO:4208), plus GE captive fiber. Shares are own estimates.
supply_tightness: Extreme concentration. SiC fiber merchant supply is essentially Japanese (NGS, Ube) plus GE captive, and it is export-controlled. CVI/MI processing know-how is proprietary. A new fiber or CMC plant takes about 3-5 years, and engine qualification of a new part takes about 5-10 years. These barriers are high, but most value is captive inside GE.
substitution_risk: Moderate on the margin. Advanced SX superalloys with better TBC/EBC and cooling can delay CMC insertion. Over the long run CMC substitutes for metal, not the reverse.
cyclicality_risk: Low to moderate. It is tied to program rates (LEAP, GE9X), so 777X slips or LEAP rate cuts flow straight through. Overbuild risk is low.
faster_sub_niche: GE9X CMC content (combustor liners, stage-1/2 HPT nozzles, shrouds) ramps from near zero after 2027 at 40%+ CAGR, but from under about $60M in 2026 (emerging). name: HEFA-SPK sustainable aviation fuel (neat SAF blendstock)
definition: IN: neat hydroprocessed esters and fatty acids synthetic paraffinic kerosene (ASTM D7566 Annex A2) sold to airlines and fuel suppliers, at neat-SAF value (including the green premium). Covers dedicated and swing HEFA units (renewable-diesel-to-SAF). OUT: co-processed SAF in fossil refineries (small), alcohol-to-jet, e-SAF/PtL (too early), renewable diesel/HVO, and fossil Jet A blended volume.
value_chain_path: Commercial aerospace -> aviation fuel -> jet fuel -> sustainable aviation fuel -> HEFA-SPK neat SAF
also_serves_megatrends: decarbonization mandates (EU, UK, Japan, Singapore, Korea, India)
size_2026_usd: US$4.5-7.5B (own estimate: 2.3-3.0 Mt x US$1.9-2.6k/t)
volume_vs_price: Almost all volume: about 30-40%/yr volume growth required by mandates. Neat-SAF price is flat to slightly down (-2% to +2%/yr), because HEFA/HVO overcapacity and Chinese UCO-based supply offset feedstock scarcity. Mandated volume makes it durable; producer margins are not durable.
math: Own estimate. 2026 volume about 2.3-3.0 Mt (IATA put 2025 at about 2 Mt, 0.7% of jet fuel). At US$1.9-2.6k/t (about 2.5-3.5x Jet A) that is about US$4.5-7.5B. 2030 mandate floor: EU 6% of about 46-50 Mt jet fuel is about 2.8-3.0 Mt (including about 0.55 Mt e-SAF, excluded here); UK 10% of about 12 Mt is about 1.2 Mt; Japan 10% target is about 1.0-1.5 Mt; Singapore, Korea, India and others about 0.5-1.0 Mt; US voluntary/45Z about 1-3 Mt; China pilots about 0.3-1 Mt. Total about 7-11 Mt in 2030. At US$1.7-2.3k/t that is US$12-25B. Supply cross-check: Neste alone has about 1.5 Mt/yr SAF capability, rising to about 2.2 Mt/yr around 2027; DGD Port Arthur adds about 0.7 Mt/yr; Montana Renewables MaxSAF expands toward about 0.9 Mt/yr by around 2028 (all company guidance, unverified).
catalyst_timing: ReFuelEU: 2% in 2025 rising to 6% in 2030 (with a 1.2% synthetic sub-mandate in 2030-31). UK mandate: 2% in 2025, 10% in 2030. Singapore levy/1% from 2026. Korea 1% from 2027. India 1% for international flights from 2027. Japan 10% target for 2030. Capacity: Neste Rotterdam expansion around 2027; DGD Port Arthur SAF (2025); TotalEnergies Grandpuits and Eni conversions (2025-2026).
key_suppliers: Neste (HEL:NESTE), about 30-40% of 2025-26 global SAF. Diamond Green Diesel (Valero NYSE:VLO / Darling NYSE:DAR). Montana Renewables (Calumet NASDAQ:CLMT). World Energy (private). Phillips 66 Rodeo (NYSE:PSX). Eni/Enilive (BIT:ENI). TotalEnergies (EPA:TTE). Repsol (BME:REP). OMV (VIE:OMV). Cosmo Oil (TYO:5021). EcoCeres (HK, private). Zhejiang Jiaao Enprotech (SSE:605077). Shares are own estimates.
supply_tightness: The feedstock is the bottleneck: UCO, tallow and distillers' corn oil are finite, and imports of Chinese UCO face fraud and tariff scrutiny. Shell paused Rotterdam and BP scaled back, so dedicated SAF capacity is thinner than announced. A new HEFA unit takes about 3-4 years. Producer pricing power holds only where mandates bind (EU, UK); in the US, OBBBA removed the SAF-specific 45Z bonus from 2026.
substitution_risk: Moderate after 2030. Alcohol-to-jet (LanzaJet) and e-SAF take share later in the decade. Co-processing in existing refineries is cheaper for small volumes. Book-and-claim schemes can shift demand geographically.
cyclicality_risk: Policy risk dominates. The US credit was cut in 2025, and EU mandate review or penalty enforcement remains uncertain. Renewable-diesel overcapacity can swing into SAF and crush margins. Price collapses in renewable fuels (2024-2025) show that revenue can lag volume.
faster_sub_niche: e-SAF/PtL grows faster in percentage terms from near zero, but it inflects only around 2029-2032 (see too_early). Within HEFA, the EU/UK-mandated volume is the faster and more durable part; US-voluntary volume is slower after the OBBBA change.

definition: IN: revenue from low-earth-orbit satellite connectivity sold to commercial airlines: per-aircraft service fees plus electronically steered antenna terminals and installation, from Starlink Aviation, Eutelsat OneWeb (via SES/Intelsat, Panasonic, Gogo etc.) and Amazon Kuiper from about 2027. size_2026_usd: US$0.6-1.2B (own estimate, low confidence)
volume_vs_price: Volume-driven: equipped aircraft grow roughly 3x from 2026 to 2030. Service revenue per aircraft is probably flat to down, because of competition (Kuiper, OneWeb Gen2) and 'free Wi-Fi' contract structures. Most of the growth is share taken from GEO IFC providers, not new spend.
math: Own estimate. Commercial aircraft on LEO: about 2,500-4,000 at end-2026 (United 1,000+, Air France, Qatar, Emirates, Alaska/Hawaiian, WestJet, airBaltic and others) rising to about 8,000-12,000 at end-2030. catalyst_timing: Fleetwide installs for United, Air France, Qatar and Emirates run 2025-2027. Amazon Kuiper aero service starts around 2027 (JetBlue launch customer, unverified). OneWeb Gen2 arrives around 2027+. Retrofit cycles are tied to C-checks over 2026-2029.
key_suppliers: SpaceX Starlink (private), about 70-85% of new LEO airline wins in 2024-26. Eutelsat OneWeb (EPA:ETL) distributed via SES/Intelsat (EPA:SESG), Panasonic Avionics (TYO:6752) and Gogo (NASDAQ:GOGO). Amazon Kuiper (NASDAQ:AMZN) from about 2027. Terminal and ESA makers: Starlink in-house, ThinKom (private), Stellar Blu (Gilat NASDAQ:GILT), Hughes (EchoStar NASDAQ:SATS). Shares are own estimates.
supply_tightness: Moderate. STC certification per aircraft type and installation-slot availability at heavy checks are the gating factors, not hardware. Starlink is effectively near-monopoly, which gives it pricing power.

name: Premium-melt (VIM/VAR/ESR) nickel-superalloy billet & PM superalloy powder for engine and IGT rotating parts
definition: IN: aerospace- and IGT-qualified, triple- or double-melted nickel (and cobalt) superalloy billet and bar (e.g., IN718, Waspaloy, 720Li) and powder-metallurgy superalloy powder/billet used for disks, shafts, rings and cases of aero engines and gas turbines. OUT: superalloy castings (see the IGT castings candidate), titanium, stainless and corrosion-resistant alloys for chemicals/oil & gas, and additive-manufacturing powders for non-engine uses.
value_chain_path: Commercial aerospace & IGT -> engines -> rotating parts (disks/shafts/rings) -> superalloy forgings -> premium-melt billet & PM powder
size_2026_usd: US$6-9B (own estimate; aero+IGT share of premium-melt superalloy mill products)
volume_vs_price: About 55-60% volume, 40-45% price. Volume grows about 5-8%/yr (engine OE plus spares, IGT). Price/mix adds about 3-5%/yr through LTAs and surcharges. The price part is shortage pricing that should ease once new melt capacity arrives around 2027-2029.

Total about $10-14B of premium alloy sales, of which aero plus IGT is about 55-65%, giving about $6-9B in 2026. At 8-13% CAGR that is about $8.5-14B in 2030.
catalyst_timing: Engine OE rate increases in 2026-2028 (LEAP above 2,000/yr, GTF Advantage, GE9X). IGT capacity doubling in 2026-2028. New melt capacity (e.g., Carpenter brownfield VIM/VAR, around FY2028, unverified) would ease tightness from around 2028.
key_suppliers: Carpenter Technology (NYSE:CRS), about 20-25% (own estimate). ATI (NYSE:ATI), about 20-25%. Special Metals / PCC (Berkshire NYSE:BRK), about 15-20%. VDM & Haynes (Acerinox BME:ACX), about 8-10%. Aubert & Duval (Airbus/Safran/Tikehau, private), about 5%. Proterial (private, ex-Hitachi Metals) and Daido Steel (TYO:5471), about 5-8%. Fushun Special Steel (SSE:600399), CISRI-Gaona (SZSE:300034), Tunan (SZSE:300855) mostly serve the China domestic market. VSMPO is sanctions-constrained (mainly titanium).
supply_tightness: Tight. VIM/VAR/ESR furnaces take about 24-36 months to deliver and commission. Customer qualification of a new melt source is about 18-36 months. Rotating-grade (LLP) material requires traceability back to the melt. Producers report record margins and multi-year LTAs (direction reported; figures unverified).
substitution_risk: Low for rotating parts. PM vs cast-wrought choice shifts share between producers within the niche. Recycled revert is already part of the melt.
cyclicality_risk: Moderate. Aero destocking (as in 2019-2020 and in parts of 2024-2025) can cut orders 20-30% in a year. Capacity added around 2027-2029 by Carpenter, ATI, Acerinox and China erodes pricing by 2029-2030.
faster_sub_niche: PM superalloy powder/billet for HPT/HPC disks (GTF Advantage, LEAP, military) may grow about 12-16%, but its size and split are unverified, and the GTF powder-metal contamination history adds qualification friction. It is not split out. This niche is a bottleneck play with pricing power, but at about 8-13% CAGR it is unlikely to rank among the economy's fastest-growing.

name: Hard carbon anode material for sodium-ion cells
definition: In scope: non-graphitizable ('hard') carbon anode active material made from biomass (coconut shell, bamboo, starch), phenolic resin, pitch or coal precursors, with roughly >280 mAh/g reversible capacity and >85% initial coulombic efficiency (ICE), qualified into sodium-ion cells. Material made captively by cell makers is valued at market price. Out of scope: soft-carbon and anthracite low-end anodes, hard carbon used as a minor fast-charge additive in Li-ion, Na-ion cathodes (Prussian white, layered oxide, NFPP), and the cells themselves (used here only to drive volume).
value_chain_path: Electrification & grid storage -> batteries -> post-lithium cell chemistries -> sodium-ion cells (ESS, 24V truck start/idle, 2-wheelers/A00 EVs, Na+Li dual-chemistry EV packs) -> anode active material -> hard carbon (precursor + carbonization/purification)
also_serves_megatrends: Grid/ESS build-out incl. AI data-center power
size_2026_usd: $150-550M (own estimate; central ~$300M): 25-50 GWh Na-ion cell output x 1.2-1.4 kt/GWh x $5-8/kg (ASP unverified)
size_2030_usd: $0.6-2.5B (own estimate; central ~$1.2-1.5B): 150-350 GWh x 1.15-1.3 kt/GWh x $3.5-5.5/kg
volume_vs_price: Growth is volume-led and therefore durable. GWh volume grows about 55-70%/yr while ASP falls about 8-12%/yr as Chinese capacity scales and precursors get cheaper. The big swing factor is the cost gap between Na-ion and LFP, which depends on the lithium carbonate price. If lithium is cheap, Na-ion volume slips by 12-18 months.
math: Intensity (own calculation): 1 kWh at ~3.1 V nominal = ~323 Ah. At ~300 mAh/g that needs ~1.08 kg of hard carbon. Adding N/P ~1.1 and ~10% first-cycle loss gives ~1.2-1.4 kg/kWh, i.e. 1.2-1.4 kt/GWh. 2026: 25-50 GWh -> 30-70 kt (incl. channel fill) x $5-8/kg = $150-560M. 2030: 150-350 GWh -> 175-455 kt x $3.5-5.5/kg = $0.6-2.5B. Cross-check against cell value: Na-ion cells at RMB 0.35-0.55/Wh x 25-50 GWh = RMB 9-27B ($1.2-3.8B) in 2026. Anode is ~8-15% of cell BOM, which is consistent. Supplier-revenue sum: not possible, because Kuraray, Kureha, BTR, Shengquan and Yuanli do not break out hard carbon (unverified).
catalyst_timing: CATL Naxtra 175 Wh/kg Na-ion cell: mass production from Dec 2025 (announced Apr 2025), plus a 24V heavy-truck starter battery. Passenger-car and ESS deployments run through 2026, and Na+Li dual-chemistry packs target 2027 models. BYD's 30 GWh Xuzhou Na-ion base (construction began Jan 2024) ramps 2026-27. Lithium carbonate has rebounded from its mid-2025 trough (~RMB 60k/t), which improves Na-ion economics. ESS safety rules favour Na-ion. Key 2027 test: whether Na-ion volume in Chinese ESS tenders exceeds ~10% share.
key_suppliers: Japan: Kuraray (3405.T, 'Kuranode' coconut-shell route) and Kureha (4023.T, pitch route). China, est. >80-90% of 2026 capacity (own estimate): BTR New Material (835185.BJ), Shanghai Putailai (603659.SS), Ningbo Shanshan (600884.SS), Shengquan Group (605589.SS, phenolic-resin route), Fujian Yuanli Active Carbon (300174.SZ, biomass), plus private players (Bosige, Jiangxi Zhengtuo) and captive supply at HiNa and Zoolnasm. No supplier discloses segment revenue; shares unverified.
supply_tightness: Nameplate capacity is probably overbuilt: Chinese announcements total hundreds of kt (unverified). The grades CATL and BYD actually qualify (high ICE >90%, low impurities, consistent precursor) are scarcer. Qualification takes 12-24 months, and precursor consistency (coconut shell supply from SE Asia, bamboo) is a real bottleneck. Pricing power is weak for commodity grades and moderate for premium grades.
substitution_risk: Medium-high. (1) Lithium relapse: if lithium carbonate falls back toward RMB 60-70k/t, LFP cells at ~RMB 0.30/Wh undercut Na-ion. (2) Soft-carbon and hard-soft blends take low-end cells. (3) High-compaction LFP and 500Ah+ ESS cells keep cutting cost. (4) Anode-free Na cells, after 2030.
cyclicality_risk: High. Chinese capacity races could repeat the 2023-24 graphite-anode price collapse. Cell makers may double-order while stocking up for 2026 launches. A lithium price whipsaw can stall adoption.
faster_sub_niche: Split into (1) ESS and truck-start grade (biomass, ~$4-6/kg; volume growth but steeper price erosion) and (2) high-ICE resin/pitch grade for EV and high-power cells (~$8-15/kg). The EV/high-power grade likely grows faster in value (50-70% CAGR, own estimate) if Naxtra passenger-car and dual-chemistry packs scale in 2027-28. Unverified.

name: CVD silicon-carbon (Si-C) composite anode material (silane deposited into porous carbon)
definition: In scope: silicon-carbon composite anode powder made by chemical-vapour deposition of nano-silicon from silane (SiH4) into a porous carbon scaffold (Group14 SCC55-type; Chinese 'new-generation CVD Si-C'). It is typically 40-55% Si with ~1,600-2,000 mAh/g, blended into graphite anodes at 5-30% by mass. The scaffold value is included. Out of scope: SiOx/pre-lithiated SiOx, ball-milled nano-Si/graphite composites, 100%-silicon anodes (Enovix, Amprius nanowire), and graphite.
value_chain_path: Electrified devices (phones, EVs, drones) -> Li-ion cells -> anode active materials -> silicon-based anodes -> CVD Si-C composite (porous-carbon scaffold + silane CVD)
also_serves_megatrends: AI smartphones/foldables (more Wh in fixed volume)
size_2026_usd: $150-500M (own estimate; central ~$250M): ~3-9 kt composite x $30-55/kg (ASP unverified)
volume_vs_price: Volume-led. Tonnes grow about 60-80%/yr while ASP falls about 10-15%/yr as silane and porous-carbon costs drop and Chinese CVD capacity scales. Content per unit rises each generation: anode Si fraction went from ~5-8% in 2024 flagships to 10-15%+ in 2025-26 high-capacity phones (per-model figures unverified).
math: Per phone (own calculation): a 25 Wh battery at 3.87 V = 6.5 Ah. With a target anode of 550-700 mAh/g and N/P 1.1, the anode needs 10-13 g of active material. Blending ~1,900 mAh/g Si-C at 13-22% gives ~1.5-3 g of Si-C per phone. 2026 phones: 400-550M Si-C phones (~33-45% of ~1.2B, unverified) -> 0.6-1.6 kt. 2026 EV and high-energy cells: 60-150 GWh at a 3-6% blend (0.03-0.06 kg/kWh) -> 2-9 kt (wide, unverified). Drones/tools/wearables: 0.3-1 kt. 2026 total ~3-9 kt x $30-55/kg = $0.1-0.5B. 2030: phones 800M-1B x 2.5-4 g = 2-4 kt; EV cells 300-700 GWh x 0.05-0.08 kg/kWh = 15-56 kt; others 2-5 kt; total ~20-65 kt x $18-30/kg = $0.4-2.0B. Key insight: phones carry the 2024-26 adoption story but are only ~$50-100M of material. EV fast-charge cells decide 2027-30 tonnage.
catalyst_timing: 2025-26: Chinese flagships moved to 7,000-10,000 mAh Si-C packs (OnePlus 15 at 7,300 mAh, Oct 2025; Xiaomi 17 Pro Max at 7,500 mAh, Sept 2025; Honor 8,000-10,000 mAh models). Next step-change: Apple and Samsung adoption in 2026-27 cycles (rumoured, unverified). Supply side: Group14 took full ownership of its Korean BAM-K plant (Aug 2025), and Sila's Moses Lake plant is starting up (company guidance). Demand side: EV fast-charge platforms adding Si-C blends in 2026-28. The REC Silicon Moses Lake shutdown (2025) tightened Western silane supply.
key_suppliers: Group14 Technologies (private; US/Korea, Sangju BAM-K). Sila Nanotechnologies (private; Moses Lake WA; its Titan Silicon process may differ from CVD-in-porous-carbon, unverified). China: BTR (835185.BJ), Ningbo Shanshan (600884.SS), Shanghai Putailai (603659.SS), Tianmu Lake Advanced Energy Materials (private), Chengdu Guibao (300019.SZ), Shenzhen XFH (300890.SZ). Porous-carbon scaffold: Shengquan (605589.SS), Fujian Yuanli (300174.SZ), Kuraray (3405.T). Silane: Henan Silane Technology (838402.BJ), SK Specialty, REC Silicon (RECSI.OL; Moses Lake idled). China est. >70% of 2026 tonnage (own estimate); shares unverified.
supply_tightness: Medium. The gating steps are CVD reactor throughput, safe silane handling (pyrophoric) and porous-carbon pore-size consistency. Qualification takes 12-24 months per cell platform. Western supply is thin after REC Silicon's Moses Lake shutdown and Group14's delay of BAM-2. Chinese capacity additions are large, so the price premium is narrowing.
substitution_risk: SiOx (better cycle life, cheaper) for EVs; high-compaction graphite plus fast-charge electrolytes; Li-metal/anode-free cells and all-solid-state batteries after 2030; 100% Si anodes in premium niches.
cyclicality_risk: High for the EV portion: Chinese overcapacity and cell-maker price squeezes. The phone portion is seasonal and concentrated in a handful of OEMs, with double-ordering risk in the 2026 phone cycle.
faster_sub_niche: Split into (1) phone-grade CVD Si-C (higher ASP, small tonnage, ~25-40% CAGR as China penetration saturates by ~2028) and (2) EV fast-charge grade (small base, 50-70% CAGR if 2027-28 platforms adopt). The EV grade is faster but less certain. The porous-carbon scaffold grows in line with the composite, so drilling further does not change the story.
